articles.title: Heidi Levine recounts how Palestinian youths helped save her in settler attack
articles.summary:
US photojournalist describes ‘protective shield’, vows to return to work in West Bank and criticises Netanyahu comments on incident

The Washington Post photojournalist who was attacked and…

blocks.text: The Washington Post photojournalist who was attacked and seriously injured by Israeli settlers on the West Bank on Friday has described how she was saved with the help of local Palestinians.

Heidi Levine sustained four fractured vertebrae, two broken ribs and four puncture wounds when she was knocked to the ground and repeatedly beaten by a crowd of masked settlers while she and other journalists were covering the olive harvest in the Palestinian village of Abu Falah, north of Ramallah.
It is unclear whether the puncture wounds were caused by knives or other weapons. Levine said a witness to her attack had seen nails sticking out of some of the wooden clubs wielded by her attackers.

Levine, 64, has covered multiple wars and had just returned from an assignment in Ukraine before Friday’s attack. She said she would most likely have been killed had she not been wearing protective body armour and a helmet.

“I probably would have been dead, because for sure it doesn’t take much to kill a person with blows to the head,” she said shortly before being discharged from hospital on Wednesday in the Israeli city of Petah Tikva.

Levine pointed out that Palestinians did not have such protection and more than 20 had been killed in settler attacks so far this year, in the course of an escalating campaign of aggression – described as terrorism by Israeli security leaders – across the West Bank aimed at driving Palestinians from their land.
“Every single journalist who looked at [the attack on me] are thinking they and I have gone to so many funerals of Palestinians killed by settlers,” Levine said.

She said the olive harvesting at Abu Falah had begun peacefully but at some point a group of young masked settlers appeared on a nearby hilltop watching the group of Palestinian villagers, journalists and human rights activists accompanying them. Levine said the attack began only after the Israeli army arrived on the scene.

“Then all hell broke loose. Some of the farmers started to gather their tarps and bags of olives that they had picked,” she said. “Then all of a sudden I hear a machine gun, and then saw teargas in the distance. I started to run … It was just like a lot of commotion and then all of a sudden I see a dozen of them and they started charging at me.

“I managed to keep my face to the ground, and I don’t know if I took that position to protect myself with my face down or it was their initial blow. Otherwise my whole face would have been broken and I could have suffered brain damage or lost an eye.
“They started kicking me and beating me with sticks. I can’t even count how many times, probably more than a hundred times. I actually tried playing dead so that they would stop. But it didn’t work.”

Witnesses said the beating only ceased when young Palestinian men used slingshots to aim stones at settlers forcing them back, allowing another American journalist, Jasper Nathaniel, to reach Levine and, with other reporters, help her to safety.
“The shabab [Palestinian youth] put themselves in front and were trying to keep them [the settlers] away, keep a protective shield, which was amazing. It was like a biblical battle,” Levine said.

After the attack, Nathaniel wrote: “Had the shabab not stepped up to protect her, she might well be dead. It is no exaggeration to say that young Palestinians armed only with stones risked their lives to save Heidi Levine’s.”

He said the army pursued the young Palestinians in the wake of the incident, rather than the settlers. Palestinians risk being shot by settlers or the soldiers if they try to resist attacks, and can face long periods in detention without charge.

Levine, who has lived in Israel for four decades, said she would go back to reporting on the West Bank as soon as she recovered. “My work is important,” she said. “They have bruised me, broken some bones, but they haven’t cracked my spirit.”
Since the attack, she has received letters from Israelis expressing regret, and an apologetic phone call from the president, Isaac Herzog.

“He was a teddy bear on the phone,” she said. “He kept saying I just want to give you a big hug and these are not representative of who this country is, they’re a dark stain, and he called them thugs.”
The office of the prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, however, put out a statement on X seeking to cast doubt on witness and video accounts of what he called an “alleged attack”.
Levine was particularly angered by Netanyahu’s claim that some video footage “appears to show Levine knocked down and immediately helped to her feet by the same unidentified individual”.

“That’s such bullshit. They helped me up because they couldn’t get my things off of me. That’s why,” Levine said. “They robbed me of everything I have – a pouch with my documents, my American passport, credit card, camera disk and a small camera bag with two other lenses. Everything is gone … That’s why [they stood me up], and then they threw me back down and continued to kick and hit me.”

The US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, called the attack a “despicable act of terror” and demanded prosecutions. Israeli police arrested 10 suspects after the Abu Salah incident and another attack on Saturday aimed at European diplomats near the West Bank village of Taybeh. Several of them were subsequently released. Prosecutions of settlers, who have allies in the army, police and Netanyahu’s cabinet, are very rare.
Asked if she expected her attackers would be brought to justice, Levine said her level of confidence was “two out of 10”.

“I am not very hopeful,” she said. “Of course, if the government made the decision to do something and crack down on this and get people arrested, they would do it. But it’s not just arresting these teenage thugs. It’s going after their leaders, the rabbis, and how they’re organised.”

articles.title: ‘You are a humanitarian also, sir’: the US feeds Putin with lies as Ukraine’s children take cover and die | Andrew Roth
articles.summary:
Steve Witkoff’s flattery of the Russian leader could be just the start of a mendacious stratagem from a US president who says Moscow ‘has been fine on Ukraine’

They say the first casualty of…

blocks.text: They say the first casualty of war is truth. For the Trump administration, the road to peace with Russia now encompasses some extraordinary lies.

Steve Witkoff delivered one as he sat down with Vladimir Putin in his native St Petersburg on Wednesday, aiming to close the deal on Russia’s land grab in Ukraine with the White House’s strategy of maximum pressure on Kyiv and saccharine flattery of the Kremlin.

“You talk so much about my president, President Trump, being a humanitarian,” said Witkoff, a real-estate mogul who, thanks to being Trump’s friend, is now the US’s senior envoy and diplomat to end the largest European conflict since the second world war. “You are a humanitarian also, sir, and I salute that. I commend you.”

In Putin’s 26 years in power, it is a rare moment when he has been granted that specific honour. Skim through Russia’s past wartime exploits, the bombing campaigns in Chechnya and Georgia and Syria, to the thousands of Russian citizens jailed for dissent, to the violent deaths of prominent opposition journalists and politicians in barely disguised assassinations and poisonings – and it will be difficult to identify Putin’s credentials as a humanitarian.

blocks.caption: Vladimir Putin and Steve Witkoff meet in St Petersburg. Photograph: Kristina Solovyova/Reuters

blocks.text: And that is before looking to Ukraine, where Russia chose to launch a full-scale invasion that has now claimed hundreds of thousands of lives. The Guardian recently obtained a Russian strategy document showing the Kremlin’s potential to black out Ukrainian cities this winter, cutting off up to 90% of electricity to cities such as Kyiv and Odesa and Kharkiv – where millions of people live – to intentionally create a humanitarian catastrophe. And judging by the nightly barrages levelled at power plants for cities across Ukraine, the Kremlin has decided to move forward with that strategy until Kyiv surrenders.

As Witkoff met Putin on Wednesday, schoolchildren in Kharkiv hustled down a reinforced stairway, sirens announcing the arrival of Shahed drones overhead. This is no ordinary bomb shelter; it is one of 10 underground schools Kharkiv has constructed because of Russia’s regular bombing of the brotherly city less than 20 miles from the border.

Parents had welcomed the schools because they were safe, said teachers, and this was the one way that young people could have an uninterrupted school day during a war that could last years more – and reignite even if a shaky peace deal is reached.

blocks.caption: Students and parents arrive and depart from the entrance to an underground school in Kharkiv. Photograph: Pete Kiehart/The Guardian

blocks.text: “We all believed in Trump. We all really had hopes for America and for Trump to stop this monster Putin,” said Olena Svytlychna, the head of the education department of the Novobavarskyi region in Kharkiv, sitting in the school’s cafe on Wednesday.
“And now we have doubts, we don’t believe them. And we are very scared.”

As Witkoff spoke, the families of six people killed in a drone strike in a park near Kharkiv this week were still holding funerals. The youngest victim of the strike was a one-year-old girl, Anhelina, who was killed as she was sitting strapped into her stroller in a playground. Her mother, Inna Mariukhna, a local schoolteacher, was also killed in the strike. The final death toll was four adults and two children, Anhelina and an 11-year-old girl.

blocks.caption: A destroyed building in Kharkiv after an air attack on Tuesday. Photograph: Sergey Bobok/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Those lives have barely earned a mention from the White House as it pushes for Ukraine to capitulate as quickly as it can this week – and crucially before the 3 November midterm elections when voters will deliver a referendum on Trump’s leadership for the last two years.

Shortly after the bombing, Trump told reporters on the White House lawn that Russia “has been fine on Ukraine”. After taking criticism for that remark, he mentioned the attacks in passing just to downplay the shelling of civilians: there were “some people in a town that got hit or whatever, but mostly young soldiers” died, he said from the Oval Office on Tuesday.

For the White House, those words cost little. Witkoff’s goal was to bring home a US citizen, a 74-year-old retired teacher from Michigan, who had been detained in Russia. But if Witkoff wants to buy a peace deal by 3 November through flattering Putin, then this will only be the White House’s opening salvo in its war on truth.

articles.title: Dancing with the Stars: Julia Stiles honours Heath Ledger with live tribute
articles.summary: If your feed is full of late '90s nostalgia and crying emojis, blame Dancing with the Stars, which during Tuesday's live dedication show, saw Julia Stiles pay tribute to her 10 Things I Hate About…

image.caption: During Tuesday's live dedication show, Julia Stiles paid tribute to her late 10 Things I Hate About You co-star Heath Ledger alongside her co-stars Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Gabrielle Union, Larisa Oleynik, Susan May Pratt and Andrew Keegan. (Disney)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New

If your feed is full of late '90s nostalgia and crying emojis, blame Dancing with the Stars, which during Tuesday's live dedication show, saw Julia Stiles pay tribute to her 10 Things I Hate About You co-star Heath Ledger.
It was a 10 Things I Hate About You reunion on Tuesday's dedication show
If your feed is full of late '90s nostalgia and crying emojis, blame Dancing with the Stars.
During Tuesday's live dedication show, Julia Stiles paid tribute to her 10 Things I Hate About You co-star Heath Ledger.
And she wasn't the only one from the 1999 teen comedy to show up to honour the late actor.

Stiles and her partner Ezra Sosa performed a contemporary routine to Can’t Take My Eyes Off You by Frankie Valli — a "no brainer" said Sosa, and a clear homage to when Ledger's character, Patrick Verona, serenades Stiles’s Kat Stratford at the end of the movie.
"When we filmed that scene the reaction on my face was totally genuine because I was so charmed by him," Stiles said of Ledger, in a video with Sosa that played ahead of the performance.
"I see pictures from that time and I'm like, wow, it was so easy with him."

Stiles said she's sad despite her "many great memories" of Ledger. "I really wish that I could pick up the phone and be like, 'Hey, dude, people really care about that movie. We did something special," she said, adding that she wanted to recreate his "lust for life."

And just like the end of the film, the end of the dance came with a treat. Sosa left Stiles on the ballroom floor as her iconic monologue from the movie played and a photo of she and Ledger was displayed overhead.
She then placed a rose underneath him before revealing her 10 Things co-stars Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Gabrielle Union, Larisa Oleynik, Susan May Pratt and Andrew Keegan, linking arm in arm with her.
Stiles and her partner Ezra Sosa performed a contemporary routine to Can’t Take My Eyes Off You by Frankie Valli. (Disney)
"I think what came up for me a lot in this dance was remembering who I was at 17 years old and who I am now." Stiles told host Julianne Hough after the routine.
"Heath just brought out the light in everybody. And he was the leader of the pack at the time. And he just made everybody else shine and feel he was always about play. We were so playful back then."

items: Julia Stiles had her Save the Last Dance moment on Dancing with the Stars
Dancing with the Stars announces next cast, including Julia Stiles and Jenna Dewan

blocks.text: Ledger died of an accidental overdose in 2008. He was 28. That year, he was awarded a posthumous Oscar for playing the Joker in Christopher Nolan's The Dark Knight.
Sosa and Stiles scored nines across the board — their highest score of the season.
Fans might hate it when a reality TV show makes them cry on a Tuesday night. But mostly, as Kat eventually said of Patrick, they don't hate it. Not even close, not even a little bit, not even at all.

Alongside Stiles, it was a night packed with other emotional tributes to the cast’s moms, wives and even other fellow co-stars. Tatyana Ali dedicated her dance to her late Fresh Prince of Bel-Air co-star James Avery, bringing along her other co-star and DWTS host Alfonso Ribeiro for the routine.
Tatyana Ali and Alfonso Ribeiro, who co-starred in The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air, paid tribute to the late James Avery. (Disney)
Ali and her partner Jan Ravnik performed a Viennese waltz to (You Don’t Know) How Glad I Am by Nancy Wilson with Ali recording her own version for the routine.
Avery, who died in 2013, played Uncle Phil on the sitcom, someone Ali said was "a father figure to all."
"It wouldn’t be the performance it needs to be without Alfonso on the stage with me."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Griffin Jaeger is a reporter and producer with CBC's entertainment unit. He also formerly hosted and produced content for The National’s digital platforms. You can reach him at griffin.jaeger@cbc.ca

articles.title: Controversial US-backed vaccine trial in African newborns halted
articles.summary:
Hepatitis B study in Guinea-Bissau that was to be funded by CDC and that drew global backlash ‘will not move forward’

The US-backed hepatitis B vaccine trial in African newborns that drew…

blocks.text: The US-backed hepatitis B vaccine trial in African newborns that drew global backlash was halted, the lead researcher said on Wednesday.

It is “now clear” that the study “will not move forward in Guinea-Bissau”, Frederik Schaltz-Buchholzer, a Danish researcher, wrote on LinkedIn, adding, “we were not given the necessary governmental approval.”
The minister of health in Guinea-Bissau, Quinhin Nantote, previously denied that the project would move forward. “This is not even remotely true,” Nantote told the Guardian in Portuguese last week.

The study was to be funded with $1.6m from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), along with another $1.6m from private partners like the Bill Ackman-backed Pershing Square Foundation and the Bluebell Foundation.

“The solution is clear here: Take the money and vaccinate as many kids as you can,” said Paul Offit, a vaccines expert at the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia, who sharply criticized the proposed study as unethical.
The government of Guinea-Bissau now has control over the researchers’ vaccines, which they apprehended when they searched the offices of the Bandim Health Project on Monday.
It is vital to support Guinea-Bissau in rolling the immunizations out to all newborns as soon as possible, Offit said. Guinea-Bissau currently plans to offer the universal birth dose in 2028.

The Danish researchers, led by Schaltz-Buchholzer, Christine Stabell Benn and Peter Aaby, hypothesized giving live vaccines, like the Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG), may have an overall mortality benefit beyond simply preventing illnesses like tuberculosis – but giving another vaccine like hepatitis B alongside it could dampen that effect.

blocks.caption: Minister of health, Quinhin Nantote, at the presidential palace in Guinea-Bissau on 29 November 2025. Photograph: Patrick Meinhardt/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Such a hypothesis is “fanciful” because the hepatitis B vaccine is a single protein among billions encountered by the immune system each day, Offit said.

“There’s no evidence for that, and it doesn’t make biological sense,” he continued. He also added that there was a very clear benefit to giving the vaccine to babies as soon as possible, because of high rates of hepatitis B in the country and the possibility of lifelong illness and death from infection.

The Danish researchers did not respond by press time to questions about the study or to this criticism. The CDC did not respond by press time to questions about whether the funding, which was appropriated through its global health work, would now be used to roll out the vaccine to all newborns in Guinea-Bissau, as recommended by the World Health Organization (WHO).

“WHO recommends that all infants receive a first dose of the hepatitis B vaccine as soon as possible after birth – preferably within 24 hours – followed by at least 2 additional doses,” said Tarik Jašarević, a WHO spokesperson. “WHO remains committed to working with national authorities, researchers, and partners to ensure that all newborns – in Guinea‑Bissau and worldwide – receive timely, evidence‑based protection against hepatitis B.”
Those who declined participation in the study would not have received the vaccines – making true informed consent impossible, experts say.

“Imagine you’re a mother. You want to do the best for your child,” said Henrik Støvring, a Danish researcher who has co-published research raising questions about previous research from the Bandim project.

“If they decide to participate in the trial, they have a 50% chance of getting the vaccine for their children. But if they stay out, they have a 0% chance of getting the vaccine. So how can you say that’s a non-coercive informed consent?” Støvring asked.

The proposed trial led to distrust among Bissau-Guineans, who wondered if the vaccine – which has a decades-long record of being safe and effective – was being tested on Africans because it was dangerous, Schaltz-Buchholzer said in his post.

It “should be clear” that both birth vaccination schedules – with or without hepatitis B – are not “dangerous to anyone”, he wrote. There is a clear benefit to giving hepatitis B vaccines at birth, and not doing so can lead to lifelong danger, experts say.
Conducting a study like this “makes the case that there’s something that’s worthy of study, for which they have no evidence,” Offit said.

“We have millions and millions, arguably hundreds of millions, of children in this world who have gotten that vaccine as a birth dose or haven’t. If there was any evidence that this was problematic, you would know this by now,” Offit added. “We eliminated hepatitis B in the United States in children virtually within years of starting that program, so the benefits are clear.”

Schaltz-Buchholzer also cast doubt on the effectiveness and safety of the hepatitis B vaccine at birth, noting that he believes the study was canceled because it challenges “prevailing medical assumptions, such as that HBV0 does not have non-specific effects”. The study, in addition to looking at mortality, would have also examined side effects like skin conditions and neurodevelopmental conditions. Dozens of studies have shown no link between vaccination and autism.

“All newborns should be given a birth dose of hepatitis B vaccine,” Offit said. “Guinea-Bissau is a country that suffers a high incidence of chronic hepatitis B. That country, more than any other country, arguably, needs to launch this program.”

articles.title: Marcos urges LGUs to improve programs for constituents
articles.summary: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Wednesday urged local government units (LGUs) to continue improving their programs to better serve their constituents.

blocks.text: Published October 22, 2026 1:16am
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Wednesday urged local government units (LGUs) to continue improving their programs to better serve their constituents.

“As the needs of our communities continue to evolve, so must the solutions we provide. Continue improving your programs. Let your accomplishments inspire other local governments to learn and to take your success even further,” Marcos said during the 2026 Galing Pook Awards: The Ten Outstanding Local Governance Programs in Malacañang.
This year’s awardees were selected following a nationwide search for outstanding local governance initiatives.

Nominees underwent a rigorous evaluation process that assessed their impact, community empowerment, innovation, adaptability, resilience, sustainability, service efficiency, and potential for replication in other areas.

Among the award-winning initiatives were Baguio City’s anti-dengue program, the use of electric vehicles in Bataan, the issuance of identification cards to residents in Lanao del Sur, Quezon City’s services for children with disabilities, and a literacy program for Mangyan communities in Oriental Mindoro.
Marcos said the initiatives demonstrated how good governance could bring meaningful change to communities.

“Magkakaiba man ang mga hamon at solusyon, iisa ang pinapakita ng mga programang ito — na ang mahusay na pamamahala ay nagdudulot ng tunay at makabuluhang pagbabago sa buhay ng ating mga kababayan,” he said.
(Although the challenges and solutions may differ, these programs demonstrate one thing: good governance brings genuine and meaningful change to the lives of our fellow Filipinos.)

“To our ten awardees, may this recognition inspire you to achieve even more. The beauty of innovation is that there is always room for improvement. Whether through technology or better approaches to governance, we can always build on what we have achieved,” he added.
Since its establishment in 1993, the Galing Pook Awards has recognized 377 programs implemented by 244 local governments. — VBL, GMA News

articles.title: BMO CEO says don't give AI agents your banking info
articles.summary: Bank of Montreal chief executive officer Darryl White says its a bad idea to give AI agents access to personal banking information like account numbers, passwords and PINs.

image.caption: BMO CEO Darryl White speaks at the Toronto Global Forum on Oct. 21, 2026. (IEFA/YouTube)

blocks.text: Business·New
Bank of Montreal chief executive officer Darryl White says its a bad idea to give AI agents access to personal banking information like account numbers, passwords and PINs.
On Tuesday, RBC's CEO said his bank may block Meta's popular Muse AI assistant
Bank of Montreal chief executive officer Darryl White says artificial intelligence agents are not to be trusted with personal banking information.

Speaking at the Toronto Global Forum on Wednesday, White expressed worry about AI advancing faster than regulations and safeguards for the technology. His remarks follow comments from RBC’s CEO on Tuesday about potentially blocking Meta’s popular Muse AI agent from accessing client data at his bank.

items: Meta's AI agent Muse set up Marketplace sale without telling him — and gave out his address

blocks.text: "We’ve grown up for 25 years in an e-commerce system where we’ve got comfortable," said White, CEO of Canada’s fourth-largest bank by total assets.
He said this has made some individuals willing to "just enter all my personal information anywhere, into any agent."
"Don't give your banking username and password. Don't give your credit card. Don't give your social insurance number. Don't give your PIN. These are not protected," White said.
"I think we've got a ways to go on educating people."

Canada’s big banks have invested billions in artificial intelligence in recent years. In August, White boasted that BMO's insurance division is using AI to make underwriting decisions in as little as 10 seconds, versus the previous industry standard of 28 days.
That perfect Ontario real estate listing might be staged by AI. Here's what to watch for

With a client’s authorization, AI agents like Meta’s Muse and OpenAI’s ChatGPT can connect to bank accounts and credit cards to monitor balances and transaction histories, and share tips on spending habits. Making purchases typically requires human approval.
On Tuesday, RBC CEO Dave McKay said his bank is considering blocking Muse from accessing client information.
"It’s something I’m thinking about, absolutely," he told Bloomberg News in a television interview.
"We’re not going to make a rash decision, but we have to balance the needs of a consumer with the privacy and safety of the system."
Last week, the CEOs of JPMorgan Chase & Co. and Charles Schwab said they are blocking or limiting outside AI agents from using their client's data.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Jeff previously worked as a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance Canada. He was also a reporter and digital producer for CTV National News, BNN Bloomberg and The Financial Post. In 2025, he was a Columbia University energy journalism fellow.

articles.title: PHP developers say key patches available after global scare
articles.summary: Newly discovered vulnerabilities in the PHP programming language have put millions of websites at risk, with government agencies across the world sounding alarm bells. PHP developers are now urging…

image.caption: PHP gaps could be used to hack government portals, small businesses and confidential databases Image: Julian Stratenschulte/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: The updates patching the recently leaked PHP security issues are now online, developers of the open-source programming language said on Wednesday afternoon.
"All PHP users are strongly encouraged to update immediately," the team said in an online statement.
Millions of websites worldwide, including critical infrastructure and government portals, as well as news sites and online shops, rely on PHP. The software is free and maintained by volunteers.

The new patches aim to fix two "critical vulnerabilities" hackers could exploit to remotely take control of websites and servers, bypassing usual obstacles such as password-protected accounts. The gaps were labeled CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619.
How did hackers trick Berlin's city government?
By exploiting them, malicious actors could gain access to government databases and customer data, deface websites, or compromise entire businesses or other online services.
Cloudflare reports 'early attacks'
The weaknesses were flagged by two separate security companies, Calif and Wiz, this August. Both of the firms used AI tools to detect the PHP issues.
PHP developers kept the flaws confidential while working on the fix. News of the security issues, however, leaked on Tuesday, a day before the scheduled update.
Hours before the PHP update, Dane Knecht, the chief technology officer of security firm Cloudflare, said hackers were already trying to exploit these weaknesses.
"We are seeing early attacks emerging and are updating mitigations as new vectors show up," he said in an online post.
Is AI the new weapon of mass data theft?
NSA urges taking websites offline if update not feasible
Authorities in multiple countries, including Australia, Japan, and several European nations, issued warnings and took down government websites in an effort to preempt potential attacks.

In France, the website of the Paris Police Prefecture was taken offline due to "detection of a critical security vulnerability," along with local government pages. Germany's government IT service took down some sites that used PHP. Belgium's Foreign Ministry temporarily blocked its own online presence, while the Dutch cybersecurity agency took itself online as a precaution.
The US National Security Agency (NSA) warned that vulnerabilities "often provide a direct path to the server's file system or database."
"If an immediate update is not feasible, it is recommend that organizations take the system offline until it can be fully mitigated," they said on X.
Meanwhile, the White House said it was informed of the issue last week and that US federal agencies were assessing the potential impact to government systems and infrastructure.

articles.title: Russia says it is ready to resume talks with Ukraine and US to end war
articles.summary: The announcement came after Russian President Vladimir Putin met US President Donald Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff in St Petersburg.

blocks.text: Russia is "ready in principle" to resume talks with the US and Ukraine on ending the conflict, Vladimir Putin's top aide has said.
Yuri Ushakov was speaking after Putin met US President Donald Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff in the Russian city of St Petersburg.

Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky and its European allies have been pressing Moscow for an immediate resumption of the talks suspended in February, and Ushakov said a new round could be held next month, possibly in Abu Dhabi.
Witkoff went to St Petersburg after meeting Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky as well as the leaders of Norway and Finland on Monday in Oslo. Ushakov said their ideas were not very "useful".
Top officials from Russia, Ukraine and the US have held several rounds of talks aimed at ending the war that began in February 2022 when Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
The talks, however, were put on hold, with the Kremlin blaming last month's "massive" Ukrainian strikes on Russia during its general elections for their disruption.
Speaking to reporters after Wednesday's talks in St Petersburg, Ushakov suggested that a new round could be held around 10 November in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates.
He stressed that the talks must focus on "building a security system for Russia and Ukraine after the end of the conflict."

A US official later told the BBC that Witkoff and Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner, another key negotiator, had proposed at Tuesday's talks in the Norwegian capital "a trilateral meeting at the technical level between the US, Russia, and Ukraine".
"This was accepted by the Ukrainians in Oslo yesterday and by the Russians in St Petersburg today," said the official, who spoke on condition of anonymity.
Ushakov also told reporters that President Putin reiterated to Witkoff that Russian troops were advancing everywhere across the vast front line and had a "strategic initiative".
Ukraine and its European allies are disputing Putin's claim, pointing to a virtual stalemate on the front.
They have also argued that the real reason of why Russia has been for months refusing to resume trilateral talks with Ukraine and the US was Putin's belief that he is winning on the battlefield.
The talks in Oslo and St Petersburg were held amid a growing row between Ukraine and the US.
Trump has said it is time for Ukraine to get a new president, and most recently "for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine".

Ahead of next month's US midterm elections, Trump has also sought to blame Ukraine's attacks on Russian oil refineries for fuel prices which have been rising since the start of the US-led war on Iran.
European leaders have expressed concern about recent US statements towards Russia.

articles.title: EXPLAINER: Who is Zofia Canlas, the new head of Presidential Commission for the Urban Poor?
articles.summary: Zofia Calnas made headlines for being a 27-year old fresh graduate who was named the new chief of the Presidential Commission for the Urban Poor (PCUP) -- but who is she?

blocks.text: Published October 22, 2026 12:15am
Zofia Calnas made headlines for being a 27-year old fresh graduate who was named the new chief of the Presidential Commission for the Urban Poor (PCUP) — but who is she?
Canlas’ appointment garnered controversy not just for her age, but for several photos showing her various travels abroad.
According to a GMA News Feed report, Malacañang had to defend Canlas, maintaining that she had long been in the PCUP.

“Tingnan po muna natin kapag nakita ninyong nagkamali at saka po tayo pumuna,” Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said in a media briefing on October 20, 2026. (Let us see first and if we see that she makes a mistake, that is when we can criticize.)
Castro said that President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. did not look at whether a person was rich or poor when appointing someone.

“Ano man ang estado mo sa buhay, mayaman ka, mahirap ka, kung ikaw ay may kakayahan na magtrabaho, magsilbi para sa bayan, iyan po ang numero uno para sa Pangulo – ang taong totoo at dedikadong may dedikasyon na makapagsilbi sa bayan,” Castro said.

(No matter what your status in life is, whether you are rich or poor, if you can work, serve the nation, that is the number one thing for the President — a person who can truly serve and is dedicated.)

The PCUP was established in 1986 through Executive Order No. 82. The PCUP is the “direct link” between the government and urban poor communities when it comes to making policies and implementing programs that would cater to the needs of the communities.
This is where much of the controversy stemmed from: Canlas seemingly has a lavish lifestyle, but her work would deal with the poor.
Prior to her post in the PCUP, Canlas was the first nominee of the Batang Quiapo Party-list; however, she was not able to secure a seat in the House of Representatives.
According to Canlas’ LinkedIn, she became a member of the PCUP in July 2025. She was the chief of staff under then-chairperson and CEO Michelle Anne Gonzales.
Another common criticism against Canlas was her high position in government despite only graduating from college two years ago in 2024.
But Castro maintained that Canlas’ age should not be judged.

“Hindi natin huhusgahan kung siya'y bata o may edad. Kung magaling, magaling… ‘Pag ang tao, may puso, bata man, may edad, kung ang tunay na pagtatrabaho ay para pagsilbihan ang mga kababayan, lalong-lalo na yung mga nasa laylayan ng lipunan,” Castro said.
(We will not judge if she is young or old. If she is good, then she is good… If a person has heart, whether young or old, the true work is to serve the nation, especially the poorest of the poor.)
Part of the PCUP’s mandate is to consult informal settler communities so that there is proper resettlement.
Despite the PCUP dealing with court decisions on these informal settlers, Castro maintained that a lawyer is not needed for the position.
Only dedication and heart are needed for the job, Castro said. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Raids at far-right group's offices at European Parliament
articles.summary: Authorities searched the Patriots for Europe's European Parliament offices in a long-running funding inquiry. The group says the charges pertain to its predecessor and there is "no legal continuity"…

image.caption: The searches appear to be part of the investigation into alleged misuse of EU funds by far-right parties or their staff during the previous legislative periodImage: Alain Rolland/Europäisches Parlament

blocks.text: The third-largest alliance of parties in the European Parliament, the right-wing nationalist Patriots for Europe (PfE) group, on Wednesday said searches had been carried out at "administrative offices" at the European Parliament buildings in Brussels and Strasbourg.
PfE said the searches appeared to be tied to the long-running probe into alleged misuse of funds by members of the now-disbanded Identity and Democracy (ID) Group.
PfE formed out of the ashes of ID, losing and gaining some members along the way, after the last European Parliament elections in 2024.
What did the investigative body say about the searches?

The European Public Prosecutor's Office — the independent body that investigates and prosecutes crimes against the EU budget, such as corruption or misuse of EU funds — said it searched premises in France and Belgium.
It said this was part of an ongoing investigation into the use of European Union funds by a former European Parliament group.
EPPO did not say which group was involved and said it would not publish further details for now for fear of compromising the investigation.
What did the PfE say about the searches?

PfE, meanwhile, confirmed the activity around its offices but also tried to stress its distance from the case since its rebrand and reformation — even though its constituent political parties are largely the same with the notable exception of the Alternative for Germany (AfD) now being excluded.

"Since this morning, the European Public Prosecutor's Office has been carrying out searches in administrative offices at the European Parliament in Brussels and Strasbourg. It would appear that these searches are linked to the complaint lodged against the Identity and Democracy Group (ID) dissolved in 2024," it wrote in a statement.
"The Patriots for Europe Group emphasizes that there is no legal continuity with the ID Group and that it is not involved in the ongoing investigations," it said.

A French member of the European Parliament for the Rassemblement National or National Rally (RN) party, Jean-Paul Garraud, said that "the offices of staff members of the former Identity and Democracy group" were targeted.
What were the details of the ID misuse of funds probe?
European Parliament auditors concluded last year that ID members had misused at least €4.3 million (roughly $4.8 million) in EU funds during the previous legislative term from 2019 to 2024.
According to their report, the money flowed to companies close to the group and to associations supporting anti-abortion campaigners.
The case was reminiscent of, but separate from, the conviction against RN leader Marine Le Pen, herself a former MEP, that for a time looked set to stifle her bid for the French presidency.
Appeals court clears way for Le Pen's presidential bid
The ID group existed for one term in the European Parliament, from 2019 to 2024. It included France's RN, Germany's AfD, Austria's Freedom Party (FPÖ) and Italy's Lega, among other members.

It fell apart after major internal friction during the 2024 European election campaign, not least because of dissatisfaction within the group with their lead candidate Maximilian Krah of the AfD over a number of issues — from controversial remarks about Nazi Germany through to allegations of his close allies being Russian and Chinese influence, with one of Krah's aides since convicted of spying for China.
RN, FPÖ and Lega are part of the new PfE group, which claims "no legal continuity" to the dissolved ID alliance, but the AfD was not invited to join the PfE.

PfE has 85 seats in the 719-seat European Parliament, making it the third-largest group in the chamber, but a rather distant third behind the center-right European People's Party (184) and the center-left Socialists and Democrats (135).
The European Parliament relies heavily on such groupings, which try to unite political parties from various member states with broadly comparable policy positions and political alignment.
The AfD set up a much smaller splinter far-right grouping called Europe of Sovereign Nations (ESN), with just 27 seats, 15 of them held by the AfD.

articles.title: Taiwan charges five men over plot to run over comedian for his Xi Jinping jokes
articles.summary:
Person named ‘K’ from China paid five defendants to injure Huang Yi-hao, New Taipei prosecutors say

Taiwanese prosecutors have charged five men over a plot to ram a car into a comedian who…

blocks.text: Taiwanese prosecutors have charged five men over a plot to ram a car into a comedian who made fun of the Chinese Communist party and Xi Jinping.
Taiwan has repeatedly accused China of transnational repression to silence critics on the self-governed island, which Beijing claims as its territory and has vowed to take by force if necessary.
In one performance, Huang Yi-hao insulted the Chinese leader’s appearance, compared him to Winnie-the-Pooh and tore into his political record.
Prosecutors in New Taipei said on Wednesday that an individual from mainland China who was identified as “K” had paid the five defendants to injure Huang badly enough to require hospitalisation.

The prosecutors said: “This case involves a serious incident in which the Chinese Communist party is suspected of using cross-border suppression tactics to direct lawless elements in our country to suppress dissenting political voices through extreme violence.”
China’s Taiwan Affairs Office did not respond to requests for comment.

A GPS tracker was allegedly put on Huang’s scooter months before the attack to identify his daily routines, Taiwan’s Central News Agency said. On 11 September, two defendants drove into Huang’s bike as he rode home, but stopped after hearing Huang scream, prosecutors said.
The comedian was left with a bruised pelvis and the suspects then allegedly pretended to help with an insurance claim in order to send a photo of Huang’s medical certificate to K.
K refused to pay the full sum of NT$450,000 (US$13,900; £10,370) promised to the suspects because Huang’s injuries were only minor, the statement said.
On Wednesday, Huang reposted a video from December 2025 in which he asked the audience to help him by shouting out the name of the person he was about to describe.

In a fast-paced diatribe, the comedian, dressed in a traditional gown, evoked “swept-back hair” and a “plump figure”, and criticised policies on Hong Kong, Covid and the property market. After finishing with an expletive, the crowd chanted back Xi’s name before breaking into applause.
In May, two people were prosecuted after spreading faeces and paint at a Taipei club hours before a Huang show.

Lev Nachman, a professor of political science at National Taiwan University, said: “It is important to remember that what we are reading about is obviously a more extreme case, but there have been threats and acts of violence against critics of the Communist party here in Taiwan for many years.”
Taiwan’s Mainland Affairs Council said in October that at least 126 individuals had been affected by Chinese transnational repression.
The Guardian has contacted the Chinese foreign ministry for comment.

In a post on Wednesday, Huang said: “If people can be subjected to this kind of treatment simply for criticising the Chinese Communist party when it does not even govern Taiwan, how can we expect to retain our current freedom of speech if the CCP were ever to rule Taiwan?”
In another post on Facebook, Huang said he would not cancel future performances but that he was “no hero”.
“I write it because it’s funny,” he said. “If I stop, it will only be because I’ve got bored of it.”

articles.title: Online sale of fake PWD IDs flagged
articles.summary: Sen. Raffy Tulfo has expressed alarm over the widespread circulation of fake identification cards for persons with disabilities sold online.

blocks.text: October 22, 2026 | 12:00am

Citing Department of Justice data, Tulfo said about eight million PWD IDs are in circulation nationwide, but only two million are legitimate and registered with the National Council on Disability Affairs.
STAR / File
MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Raffy Tulfo has expressed alarm over the widespread circulation of fake identification cards for persons with disabilities (PWDs) sold online.

“Those suffering most are people with legitimate disabilities who should benefit from the 20 percent discount and small businesses who shoulder additional expenses,” Tulfo said during yesterday’s deliberations on the proposed 2027 budget of the Department of Social Welfare and Development.
Almost P166 billion in losses have been reported, particularly in the restaurant industry, amid the proliferation of fake PWD IDs.
Tulfo said it contributed to growing public skepticism toward people presenting PWD IDs to claim discounts.
Reports of widespread online selling of fake IDs on Facebook Marketplace and Carousell were verified by Tulfo.
His Senate team interviewed David Sison, president of RESTOPH, an association of restaurant owners in the Philippines.
Sison recounted an instance wherein every member of a family, including the mother, father, children and household helper, reportedly possessed a PWD ID.
Verifying the authenticity of PWD IDs is difficult, Tulfo pointed out.
Although the Department of Health maintains a website for verification, he said its information is outdated.
More than 2,500 local government units issued PWD IDs nationwide, yet their designs, formats and databases are not standardized, making verification more challenging, he noted.
Requirements for issuing PWD IDs must be reviewed, Tulfo stressed.
Tulfo called for clearer criteria on which disabilities qualify people for the ID to prevent abuse of the system and ensure that benefits reach those who need them.

articles.title: ICC prosecutor updates trial brief vs Duterte
articles.summary: The prosecutor of the International Criminal Court has filed a revised trial brief detailing the charges of crimes against humanity against former president Rodrigo Duterte.

blocks.text: October 22, 2026 | 12:00am
Photos courtesy of the International Criminal Court show former president Rodrigo Duterte during his first in-person appearance before the tribunal since his arrest in March 2025.
Photos / ICC | via Janvic Mateo

MANILA, Philippines — The prosecutor of the International Criminal Court (ICC) has filed a revised trial brief detailing the charges of crimes against humanity against former president Rodrigo Duterte.

Acting prosecutor Mame Mandiaye Niang filed the updated trial brief on Oct. 16 after the ICC Trial Chamber III denied the inclusion of one incident that the Office of the Prosecutor wanted to add to the charges.

“The prosecution has removed all references to Incident 57 in the Trial Brief and replaced them with ‘(DELETED)’ in order to retain cross-references,” read the three-page filing released on Wednesday.

“No amendments have been made to the prosecution’s List of Witnesses or its List of Evidence,” it added, stating that those relating to the removed incident is still relevant to the charges, particularly the “contextual elements of crimes against humanity and Mr. Duterte’s individual criminal responsibility.”
The incident was supposed to be included in the charges involving alleged murder of high-value targets, but falls outside the confirmed charges “of between around July 2016 and July 2017.”
Records show that it occurred “two weeks after” the covered period.

MANILA, Philippines — State weather forecasters have declared Super Typhoon Rosal as the “strongest” tropical cyclone so far this year as it reached its peak.
Rosal reached this peak late Tuesday evening.
As of 4 p.m. yesterday, Rosal was located 750 kms east of Aparri, Cagayan, packing winds of 205 kph and gusts of 250 kph.
Tropical cyclone wind signal No. 2 is raised in Batanes.
Wind signal No. 2 is also hoisted in Cagayan including Babuyan Islands, eastern portion of Isabela, Ilocos Norte, Apayao and the northeastern portion of Catanduanes.
Experts warned that wind signal No. 3 is still expected to be raised in the next few days.
Rosal is anticipated to be downgraded to a typhoon today and exit the Philippine area of responsibility by late Friday or early Saturday.
Landfall is still less likely as it moves northwest over the Philippine Sea, according to the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration.
Malacañang gave assurance that the social welfare, health and environment departments are ready for Rosal.
“If there are heavy rains in your area, it may be an opportunity to collect rain water if your place is experiencing a dry spell,” Palace press officer Claire Castro said yesterday. – Alexis Romero

articles.title: Pinoys split on Sara’s impeachment – OCTA
articles.summary: Although some Filipinos have already taken a stand on the ongoing impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, most believe it is still too early to decide how senators should vote, according to…

blocks.text: October 22, 2026 | 12:00am
Vice President Sara Duterte arrives at the Senate in Pasay City on July 7, 2026 to meet with members of her defense team ahead of the continuation of her impeachment trial.
The Philippine STAR / Ryan Baldemor

MANILA, Philippines — Although some Filipinos have already taken a stand on the ongoing impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, most believe it is still too early to decide how senators should vote, according to OCTA Research.
Results of the Sept. 28 to Oct. 4 survey conducted by OCTA found that 47 percent of respondents want more evidence before taking a stand on Duterte’s impeachment.
Twenty-one percent said the Senate impeachment court should vote to convict Duterte, while 25 percent said senators should acquit her.
More respondents now support either conviction or acquittal compared to a similar poll conducted in July.

OCTA said support for conviction among respondents in Metro Manila rose significantly from 19 percent in July to 34 percent, while support for acquittal among those in Mindanao increased from 41 percent to 52 percent.
OCTA said the findings suggest that a verdict “is unlikely by itself to end the political conflict surrounding the case.”

In a separate development, Malacañang yesterday laughed off Duterte’s call for the government to “start working and stop politicking,” saying she was the one who undertook several personal foreign trips while President Marcos was dealing with the country’s problems. – Alexis Romero

articles.title: Palace: Probe possible lapses in Atong Ang’s escape
articles.summary: Malacañang has called for an investigation to determine whether there were lapses that allowed businessman Charlie “Atong” Ang to leave the Philippines, as the government seeks to…

blocks.text: October 22, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang has called for an investigation to determine whether there were lapses that allowed businessman Charlie “Atong” Ang to leave the Philippines, as the government seeks to strengthen border security to prevent fugitives from escaping authorities.
Palace press officer Claire Castro said negligence could not yet be concluded until the investigation is completed.
“We have to investigate whether there were lapses. There are people who are quick to flee and this is not the first time that Atong Ang escaped,” Castro told a press briefing yesterday.
Castro said efforts to secure the country’s borders should be strengthened, noting that fugitives could escape through backdoor exits because the Philippines is surrounded by bodies of water.
She also urged the public not to help fugitives evade authorities.

Asked whether the government was coordinating with foreign counterparts to track Ang, Castro said authorities would take all necessary steps in accordance with the law, following President Marcos’ directive.
Castro assured the families of the missing cockfighting enthusiasts that efforts to locate Ang were underway.
Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla revealed on Monday that Ang had left the country.
He maintained yesterday that intelligence reports of his escape underwent extensive validation for about a year before he disclosed the information.
Remulla added that much of the information came from Ang’s former cohorts, who have turned state witnesses against him.
“Validation takes a while. Upon taking all the intelligence reports, our theory is that he left the country,” Remulla said.

His statement yesterday came as Justice Secretary Fredderick Vida said the Bureau of Immigration has no record of Ang leaving the country. Remulla, however, said Ang is believed to have slipped out through unofficial means.
Ang, accused of masterminding the kidnapping and killing of cockfight enthusiasts or sabungeros, is believed to be in Cambodia.
‘Surrender, Bato’
Meanwhile, Malacañang urged yesterday Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa to turn himself over to authorities as it expressed alarm over the possibility of bloodshed should force be used to arrest him.
Remulla recently said that Dela Rosa, who has been accused of crimes against humanity related to the drug war, is being protected by a powerful group in Mindanao.
Dela Rosa’s protectors include armed men and a confrontation could result in fatalities worse than that of the 2017 Marawi siege, Remulla said.
“Surrender to avoid a bloodshed,” Castro said. - Ghio Ong

articles.title: Reckless decisions on China row must be avoided – Palace
articles.summary: Malacañang won’t stop lawmakers from issuing resolutions against China’s ambassador even as it cited the need to avoid reckless decisions in the face of the tense exchanges between…

blocks.text: October 22, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang won’t stop lawmakers from issuing resolutions against China’s ambassador even as it cited the need to avoid reckless decisions in the face of the tense exchanges between the Chinese embassy and some Philippine officials.

“If you are angry, you cannot think properly although our feelings are valid. We have countrymen in China we have to protect. Our President does not back out and does not abandon our rights. As to how it can be implemented to protect our country, this will be discussed. We should not be reckless in any decision,” Palace press officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said yesterday.

“The DFA (Department of Foreign Affairs) has spoken and (it) did not like the response of the ambassador of China. So whatever appeal will be made, whatever action will be undertaken by the Senate and (the House), the President will not stop it.”
Castro said some people have adopted “extreme” views about the issue, but they cannot be blamed because the “visitor” is not treating the residents of the country well.
She said President Marcos has not met with Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan, who has earned the ire of some lawmakers because of what they described as his rude and threatening statements.

Castro added that the exchanges between the ambassador and some Philippine officials should not divert attention away from the claim that businesses linked to Vice President Sara Duterte have received Chinese money.
In an interview yesterday with “Storycon” on One News, Defense Secretary Gilbert Teodoro accused the Chinese embassy of interfering in local affairs, including politics.
“We can say that this is already interference in our country’s internal affairs, because they are turning this into a political issue and capitalizing on it,” Teodoro said.

“This is what our people need to understand. They are interfering in our politics because they are handling the matter in a way that has made it political. Their language is no longer diplomatic,” he added.
The defense chief did not discount the possible impact of China’s actions in the upcoming 2028 election, noting how the embassy “transformed” its messaging to something that is more aggressive.
“It has become a political fight, not a diplomatic one. Their statements are now about our internal politics,” he said.

“The threat there is the continuing attempt to expand sa West Philippine Sea,” he said. “The major issue here is their attempt to seize our territory. We should not allow ourselves to be distracted from that.”
Playing tit-for-tat, the Chinese embassy said Filipinos – especially politicians and lawmakers – who want Jing out are not welcome in China either.
“Since you don’t welcome us, we don’t welcome you, either. Fair enough,” the Chinese embassy said in a post on Facebook.
This developed as 10 more members of both the administration and minority blocs in the House of Representatives joined senators in urging President Marcos to declare Jing persona non grata.
The lawmakers crossed party lines in filing House Resolution 1562 persuading the Chief Executive to expel Jing or seek his recall by the Chinese government.

“The President, being vested with executive power, holds primary authority to conduct foreign relations and to represent the nation in its dealings with other states and must therefore take decisive action in response to statements and conduct that undermine national sovereignty and threaten the country’s security,” a portion of the three-page resolution read.

The House members who signed the resolution were Reps. Ziaur-Rahman Alonto Adiong (Lanao del Sur), Adrian Michael Amatong (Zamboanga del Norte), Kaka Bag-ao (Dinagat Islands), Leila de Lima (Mamamayang Liberal), Akbayan party-list Reps. Chel Diokno, Percival Cendaña, and Dadah Kiram Ismula; Cielo Krisel Lagman (Albay), Karl Fernandez Legazpi (Pinoy Workers) and Mark Anthony Santos (Las Piñas).
Vice President Sara Duterte’s spokesman Paolo Panelo, meanwhile, insisted she is not siding with China in its ambassador’s verbal spat with Philippine officials.
Duterte’s position is “to bring the temperature down, to de-escalate the tension” and let the DFA resolve the issues with China, Panelo said. – Janvic Mateo, Pia Lee-Brago, Evelyn Macairan

articles.title: Comelec delists Bayan, 49 other party-list groups
articles.summary: The Commission on Elections (Comelec) has canceled the registration of 50 party-list groups, including Bayan Muna, Magdalo and Buhay, over failure to meet participation or electoral performance…

blocks.text: Headlines
October 22, 2026 | 12:00am

The Comelec formalized the action through Resolution 11281, which covers party-list groups, organizations and coalitions that failed to participate in the last two preceding elections or meet the applicable requirements for obtaining seats under the party-list system.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — The Commission on Elections (Comelec) has canceled the registration of 50 party-list groups, including Bayan Muna, Magdalo and Buhay, over failure to meet participation or electoral performance requirements.

Ten of the groups were cited for not participating in the two preceding elections. These are 1 Alliance Advocating Autonomy Party, 1-United Transport Koalisyon, Agbiag Timpuyog Ilocano Inc., Ako Ayoko sa Bawal na Droga, Filipino Family Party, Grains Retailers’ Confederation of the Philippines Inc., Ina Na Nagmamahal sa Anak, Isang Lapian ng Mangingisda Bayan Tungo sa Kaunlaran, Luntiang Pilipinas Partylist and One Philippines.

The other groups are the Advocacy for Teachers Empowerment Through Action Cooperation and Harmony Towards Educational Reform, Advocates & Keepers Organization of OFWs Inc., Advocates for Retail, Fashion, Textile, Tradition, Events & Creative Services Sector (ARTE), Ahon Mahirap, formerly Partido COCOMAN, Ako Padayon Pilipino (AKO PADAYON), Aktibong Kaagapay ng mga Manggagawa (AKTIBONG KAAGAPAY), Alliance for Resilience, Sustainability and Empowerment (ARISE), Alyansa Laban sa Substance Abuse Para sa Bagong Pilipinas Natin, Ang Komadrona Inc. (ANG KOMADRONA), Ang Programang Aasenso Taumbayan-Dream, Act, Participate and Advocate for Sustainable Transformation (APAT-DAPAT), Ang Bumbero ng Pilipinas (ABP), Ang Pamilya Muna (PAMILYA MUNA), Babae Ako Para Sa Bayan Inc. (BABAE AKO), Banat Barangay Natin, Bayan Muna (BAYAN MUNA), Bayaning Tsuper (BTS BAYANING TSUPER) and Bisaya Gyud Party-list (BG PARTY-List).

Also included are BOSES party-list, formerly MOCHA; Buhay Hayaan Yumabong (BUHAY); Bunyog (Pagkakaisa); Computer Literacy, Innovation Connectivity and Knowledge Inc. (CLICK PARTY); Democratic Independent Workers’ Association (DIWA); Filipino Rights Protection Advocates of Manila Movement (FRONTLINERS ANG BIDA); Health, Education, Livelihood Program of the Philippines (H.E.L.P. PILIPINAS); Hugpong Federal Movement of the Philippines Inc. (HUGPONG FEDERAL); Ipatupad for Workers Inc. (IPATUPAD); Lungsod Aasenso Inc. (LUNAS); Magdalo Para Sa Pilipino (MAGDALO); Maharlikang Pilipino Party (MAHARLIKA); Mindanao Indigenous Peoples Conference for Peace and Development (EPANAW SAMBAYANAN); Movement of Active Apostolic Guardians Association of the Philippines (MAAGAP); Pamilyang Magsasaka; Pinoy Ako; Rebolusyonaryong Alyansang Makabansa (RAM); Towards Development and Action (TODA AKSYON); Tulong Ipamahagi sa Communidad Tungo sa Kaunlaran (TICTOK); Tulungan Tayo; Truism Isulong Mo (TURISMO); United Frontliner’s of the Philippines; and Walang Iwanan sa Free Internet Inc. (WIFI).
The cancellation is anchored on Republic Act 7941 or the Party-List System Act and the rules under Comelec Resolution 11204 as amended.

Section 6(8) of the law authorizes the poll body to cancel a party-list group’s registration, after due notice and hearing, either on its own initiative or upon a verified complaint from an interested party, for failure to participate in the two preceding elections or failure to obtain the required votes in the relevant elections.
The action forms part of the Comelec’s implementation of the rules governing the registration and continued participation of organizations in the party-list system.

articles.title: DICT exec suspended over P1.5 billion contracts
articles.summary: An undersecretary of the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) has been suspended for six months by the ombudsman for allegedly awarding contracts worth P1.55 billion to…

blocks.text: October 22, 2026 | 12:00am

DICT Undersecretary David Almirol Jr. founded Multisys Technologies Corp. in 2010 and served as its president and chief executive officer for more than a decade, the Office of the Ombudsman disclosed.
BusinessWorld / DICT Facebook page

MANILA, Philippines — An undersecretary of the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) has been suspended for six months by the ombudsman for allegedly awarding contracts worth P1.55 billion to companies linked to a firm he founded.
Eight contracts related to the rollout of the eGovPH Super App were awarded to “companies with financial relationships with Multisys” from November 2023 to May 2025, the Office of the Ombudsman said.
Almirol did not divest immediately after his appointment in the DICT in August 2022, it noted.

“Respondent was still listed as a stockholder of Multisys holding 49.21 percent of the stocks,” the ombudsman said, citing Multisys’ general information sheet received by the Securities and Exchange Commission in November 2022.

According to the ombudsman, the contracts “covered information and communications technology consultancy, e-government application deployment, web-based messaging services, cloud infrastructure, data center colocation and software subscriptions.”

Almirol will undergo “preventive suspension for six months without pay pending the resolution of administrative complaints of grave misconduct, conduct prejudicial to the best interest of the service and violation of the code of conduct and ethical standards for public officials and employees,” the ombudsman said yesterday.

articles.title: Indian court orders release of two leaders of Cockroach movement
articles.summary:
Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka spent a week in jail after defying restrictions on protests in Delhi amid government crackdown

An Indian court has ordered the release of two leaders of India’s…

blocks.text: An Indian court has ordered the release of two leaders of India’s Cockroach movement who were jailed last week amid a mounting state crackdown on youth-led protests.
The two leaders of the Cockroach Janta party (CJP) movement, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, had spent a week in Delhi’s Tihar jail after being arrested by Delhi police last week.
On Wednesday, a special magistrate ordered that Das and Ranka be released, despite efforts by police to keep them in prison. They were made to sign a bond pledging no further breach of peace.

Their arrest came after a draconian police crackdown on a CJP march held in the capital two weeks ago to protest alleged manipulation of the country’s electoral roll, which led to the barricading of central Delhi and thousands of young people being detained.
Das and Ranka were taken into custody for a second time days later after they jumped police barricades and held up an Indian flag at a site in central Delhi that police had cordoned off.

The pair were charged with trespass and violating the peace and sent to jail for five days, which was then extended by two further days. Their detention had provoked outrage among leaders and supporters of the youth movement, who accused the government of “cowardice” for jailing CJP leaders for holding a peaceful protest.
After the magistrate’s ruling on Wednesday evening, Das said that “truth has triumphed”.
The release of the two leaders is likely to come as a blow to the ruling Narendra Modi government, which has implemented an unforgiving crackdown on recent protests that have erupted across India.

The CJP, alongside the opposition alliance, student groups and civil society, have been calling for the resignation of the chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, who is accused of overseeing a revision of the electoral roll that benefits Modi’s Bharatiya Janata party (BJP) and has led to more than 130 million names being deleted from the voter register. The BJP has denied any interference.

The CJP began as an online satire earlier this year, but has since grown into a fully fledged political movement, challenging the powerful Modi government. Over the summer, it was Cockroach-led protests that forced the resignation of Modi’s education minister after sustained demonstrations.

Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of the CJP movement, vowed over the weekend that the Modi regime and threat of jail would not intimidate the Cockroaches. Dipke was also detained on Friday after he called for a peaceful demonstration in central Delhi where CJP supporters would gather and wave the Indian flag in solidarity with Das and Ranka.
He had said that, once his fellow Cockroach leaders were released, they would “gather, re-strategise, and determine how to move forward”.

“The illegal arrests and detentions we have witnessed over the past few days indicate an attempt to intimidate us,” said Dipke. “But we will not be cowed down or retreat. This is a long battle and we are prepared for it.”

articles.title: Putin orders release of jailed American as he meets Trump envoy for Ukraine talks
articles.summary: Russia frees Stephen Hubbard after US request while Steve Witkoff praises Putin, wanted by ICC as war criminal, as a ‘humanitarian’

blocks.text: Vladimir Putin ordered the release of an American from a Russian jail as he met Donald Trump’s envoy Steve Witkoff in St Petersburg on Wednesday for fresh talks on ending the war in Ukraine, amid increasingly close relations between Moscow and Washington.
Trump had previously asked Putin to free Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old former teacher who had spent more than four years in Russian jails on charges of fighting as a mercenary for Ukraine.

His release appeared to be Moscow’s latest calculated move to bring Trump further into line with Putin’s position on Ukraine, while offering the US president a diplomatic victory before the midterm elections.
Hubbard was released unilaterally by Russia, rather than as part of a prisoner exchange as has often been the case with previous releases of Americans held in the country.
Writing on social media after the release was announced, Trump said it followed a request he had made “directly” to Putin last week.

He wrote on Truth Social: “The United States, out of respect for President Trump, was not required to give anything in return – an unprecedented situation for Russia … There was no ‘swap’ necessary for this release.”

blocks.caption: Stephen Hubbard in court in Moscow in October 2024. Photograph: Moscow city court press service/AP

blocks.text: Witkoff, meanwhile, lavished praise on Putin during their meeting at the grand Constantine Palace in St Petersburg, describing the Russian president as a humanitarian.

“You talk so much about my president, President Trump, being a humanitarian. You are a humanitarian also, sir, and I salute that,” Witkoff told Putin. He also conveyed Trump’s thanks for a deal to resume Russian diesel exports to the US.

The Russian president is wanted by the international criminal court (ICC) as a war criminal, in relation to the deportation of Ukrainian children to Russia during the war. More than 17,500 civilians have been confirmed killed in Ukraine since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022, according to the UN, which says the true toll is likely to be significantly higher.

The warmth of Witkoff’s remarks stood in stark contrast to the increasingly hostile rhetoric directed at Volodymyr Zelenskyy by senior US officials, most notably Trump, who has called for the Ukrainian president to resign and portrayed him as the main obstacle to peace.

Witkoff travelled to Russia from Oslo, where he had met Zelenskyy and European leaders a day earlier in an attempt to inject momentum into stalled negotiations, with Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine now in its fifth year.

Witkoff told Putin during a televised portion of their meeting: “We’ve brought some papers. It’s really some ideas, some sort of peace deal between Russia and Ukraine, and you’ll read that at your leisure.”
The visit was Witkoff’s ninth to Russia since Trump tasked him with brokering an end to the war.

blocks.caption: ‘You are a humanitarian also, sir, and I salute that,’ Witkoff told Putin during their meeting. Photograph: Kristina Solovyova/Pool Sputnik Kremlin/AP

blocks.text: The latest rupture in relations between Washington and Kyiv was triggered by Trump’s surprise decision to lift sanctions on Russian diesel as part of a deal with Putin, followed by his call for Zelenskyy to be replaced after Ukraine refused to halt its strikes on Russian oil refineries.
Kyiv has since complained of disruptions to US intelligence-sharing and restrictions on its access to Starshield, the military-grade version of Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite network.
Zelenskyy said on Tuesday that Washington had resumed providing advance warnings of Russian missile attacks after his meeting with Witkoff in Oslo.
after newsletter promotion

But Ukraine continues to face restrictions on Starshield, although it remains unclear who ordered them. The Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday that Musk had personally ordered the slowdown, while Reuters, citing sources, said the directive had come from inside the White House.

During Wednesday’s meeting with Witkoff, Putin thanked Trump and his wife, Melania, for “their attention to efforts to end the war”. Witkoff said there was “some degree of momentum” behind efforts to reach a peace deal, describing the talks in Oslo as “constructive”.

Yet there are few signs of an imminent breakthrough. Despite repeated Ukrainian calls for a ceasefire, including a halt to attacks on energy infrastructure, Moscow has given little indication that it intends to end its bombardment of Ukraine as winter approaches, apparently confident that continued pressure will help it extract greater concessions from Kyiv.
The Russian leader remains intent on sticking to his maximalist war aims, including his demand for full Russian control of Ukraine’s eastern Donetsk region.

After the Witkoff meeting, the Kremlin said it was open to new three-way peace talks between Russia, Ukraine and US, which could take place ⁠in Abu Dhabi and would be focused on how to guarantee the security of Ukraine and Russia once the war ended.

Putin also sought to emphasise the prospects for closer economic ties between Russia and the US once the war ends, suggesting that Moscow could significantly increase its exports of fertilisers to the American market.
Russian officials said the first tanker carrying diesel to the US would depart on Thursday as part of an initial shipment of about 300,000 tonnes.

Energy analysts and traders have questioned whether Trump’s agreement to temporarily resume Russian diesel imports will deliver meaningful relief to US consumers before the midterm elections, arguing that the volumes involved are too small to significantly ease the global supply squeeze.

The talks on Wednesday also touched on a possible meeting in China next month between Putin, Trump and the Chinese president, Xi Jinping. The Kremlin said Beijing was already making preparations for what it described as an unprecedented summit between the three leaders.
