articles.summary: Senator Robin Padilla urged detractors to talk to Chinese ambassador Jing Quan, maintaining that the envoy did not issue any threats to the Philippines.

blocks.text: Published October 21, 2026 11:09pm
Senator Robin Padilla urged detractors to talk to Chinese ambassador Jing Quan, maintaining that the envoy did not issue any threats to the Philippines.

In a “24 Oras” report by Ian Cruz on Wednesday, Padilla was seen mingling with Quan at the ASEAN-Chinese Business Leaders Summit. The senator described the Chinese envoy as an “educated gentleman” despite his seemingly threatening remarks against the Philippines.

“Anong basehan ko? Nakausap ko nang personal eh. Yun ang pagkakaiba kapag nagkakausap tayo nang personal. Hindi yung nag-uusap tayo, mayroon pasakalye, puro komento. Walang madadale doon. Kailangan kung may issue ka sa tao, kausapin mo nang personal para makilala mo,” Padilla said in an interview after his initial statements.

(What was my basis? I talked to him personally. That is the difference if you talk personally. Not talking through the streets, or through comments. That will not get anywhere. If you have an issue with someone, you should talk personally to get to know them.)
Asked if Padilla brought up Quan’s controversial remarks, Padilla said that their talk was cut short.
“Never silang nagbanta. Walang ganoon. Tayo lang na yung mga…ang advice ko na lang sa mga sobrang tapang na mga kababayan natin. Kausapin niyo na personal, tutal matapang kayo,” Padilla said.
(They never threatened. There is nothing like that. We are the ones… my advice for our citizens that are so tough. Talk to them personally since you are so brave.)
Before this, Philippine Coast Guard spokesperson for the West Philippine Sea Commodore Jay Tarriela questioned Padilla’s definition of being educated.

“For the past months since he became the ambassador, we saw all the things he said on social media and the most recent one where he threatened our Filipino citizens that if they use force, they will win and the Philippines will lose,” Tarriela said in a mix of English and Filipino.
Tarriela also questioned sentiments that the Chinese side only needed to be spoken to—Quan had issued those statements in person.

“Does this kind of personality represent what Senator Robin Padilla was saying of a proper person? … It depends on their level of closeness. Maybe the reason why he has this kind of conversation with the Chinese Ambassador is that they are really close on a personal level,” Tarriela said.—Jean Mangaluz/LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Poland’s parliament votes to ease abortion ban but faces likely veto from president
articles.summary:
Measures would remove some penalties for those helping women access abortion but are ‘small-scale step’, say campaigners

Poland’s lower house of parliament has approved two bills aimed at…
articles.byline: Ashifa Kassam European Community affairs correspondent

blocks.text: Poland’s lower house of parliament has approved two bills aimed at loosening a near-total ban on abortions, in what campaigners have described as a “small-scale step” ahead of protests calling on the government to fulfil its promises to overhaul the country’s laws.

The new measures, which are likely to be vetoed by Poland’s nationalist president, would remove some of the criminal penalties for those who help women to access abortion care and allow terminations in cases of foetal abnormalities.

Leah Hoctor, of the Center for Reproductive Rights, said: “These bills represent a very small-scale change. Even if these pieces of legislation are ratified and signed into law by the Polish president – which remains to be seen – they would change very little for most women in Poland who need abortion care.”

This view was echoed by the NGO Legalna Aborcja (Legal Abortion), a reproductive rights and advocacy initiative. “What does this mean for women who need an abortion right now? Nothing, because none of these bills would help them,” said a spokesperson.

The Fundacja Widzialne (Visible Foundation) asked people to keep up the pressure on the government by taking to the streets on Thursday. “Poland still has an inhumane abortion law,” it wrote on social media as it announced rallies in 27 cities. “We demand the full decriminalisation of abortion and access to abortion covered by the National Health Fund!”

The rallies, backed by a range of groups across Poland, mark the sixth anniversary of a 2020 ruling that tightened the country’s already-restrictive abortion rules. The ruling prompted the largest protests in Poland since the fall of communism as people poured into the streets wielding placards that read “The revolution has a uterus” and “My body, my choice”.

blocks.caption: People in Warsaw protest against strict anti-abortion laws in 2023. Photograph: Anna Liminowicz/The Guardian

blocks.text: The protests were later credited with helping to propel Donald Tusk into power in 2023, with promises to overhaul abortion laws within 100 days. Last year Tusk backtracked on the pledge to legalise abortions until the 12th week of pregnancy, saying there was “simply no majority” to reform the laws.

Even if the two bills passed this week are signed into law, Poland would remain “completely out of step with the rest of its EU peers”, said Hoctor. Currently, abortion is only legal in Poland when a pregnancy results from a criminal act, such as rape or incest, or when it threatens the life or health of the mother.
after newsletter promotion

The Center for Reproductive Rights instead called on Tusk to skirt around Poland’s polarised politics by putting in place an interim moratorium on the application of all criminal law provisions concerning abortion. “This would ensure that those caring for women no longer do so under the threat of criminal investigation and prosecution,” Hoctor said.

The idea was first floated by the UN Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination against Women, which in 2024 concluded that women in Poland faced severe human rights violations due to restrictive abortion laws.

Hoctor said: “The reality is that thousands of women in Poland every year access abortion care. So they are doing that illegally, or they’re travelling for it. That’s not what a modern European country needs to be. They’re not living up to the promise of what it is to be a modern healthcare system and a modern democracy.”

articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte"s spokesperson clarified that her “troublemaker” comments did not signify that she sided with China.

blocks.text: Published October 21, 2026 10:33pm
Vice President Sara Duterte’s spokesperson clarified that her “troublemaker” comments did not signify that she sided with China.
In a "24 Oras" report from Marisol Abdurahman on Wednesday, the vice president’s spokesperson Paolo Panelo said that her comment was in relation to the Laos-Philippine drug bust.

“Ang konteksto noon is ‘yung nasabat na illegal drugs sa Laos, ‘yung papunta dapat ng Pilipinas…tapos ginamit ito ni Secretary Gibo Teodoro itong troublemaker na statement ni VP Sara, ginamit niya naman sa anti-China rhetoric niya,” Panelo said.
(The context of that was the illegal drugs in Laos, the one headed to the Philippines… then the troublemaker statement of VP Sara was used by Secretary Gibo Teodoro for his anti-China rhetoric.)
Teodoro had slammed Duterte’s troublemaker comments, saying that China was the true troublemaker.
Panelo called Teodoro’s response politicking.
“Kapag ang mga politiko ay pinopolitika itong China issue, ang tatamaan niyan hindi naman sila kundi ‘yung mga ordinaryong Pilipino at ‘yung mga negosyong umaasa sa ugnayan sa China,” Panelo said.
(If politicians politicize this China issue, it is ordinary Filipinos who are affected, the Filipinos whose businesses rely on China.)
Duterte and her husband, lawyer Manases Carpio, have been accused of receiving money from China through their organizations.
Panelo said the allegations are without basis.

"May donation ng Chinese government sa Tapangin at Malasakit [Foundation], and the Vice President is one of the trustees. Awtomatikong agad na sinusuportahan ng Chinese government si Vice President?" he said.
"What if it was used to build classrooms? Or what if it was used for charitable purposes at may resibo?" he added. —Jean Mangaluz/LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Where in the world is Atong Ang? Is he in the Philippines or not?
articles.summary: But whether or not Ang has already left the country, one thing remains unchanged: the police have failed and continue to fail to locate and arrest the fugitive

blocks.text: But whether or not Ang has already left the country, one thing remains unchanged: the police have failed and continue to fail to locate and arrest the fugitive
After months of dead silence, the Philippine government again mentioned the name of fugitive and gaming tycoon Charlie “Atong” Ang.
But this time around, it’s because the tycoon might have already left the country.
Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) chief Juanito Victor “Jonvic” Remulla refused to provide more details regarding Ang’s supposed exit.
“Wala na (Nothing). I have nothing to add,” said Remulla on Tuesday, October 20.
“He has used the backdoor [exit]. Yes, the backdoor,” the DILG chief later confirmed.

Ang has a pending warrant of arrest from Santa Cruz, Laguna Regional Trial Court Branch 26 due to his kidnapping with homicide cases related to the missing sabungeros (cockfighting enthusiasts) controversy. He has yet to be arrested since his warrant’s issuance in January.

But there seems to be confusion within the administration of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. in so far as Ang’s case is concerned. Apparently, the Department of Justice (DOJ) believes — at least based on available records — that the fugitive is still in the country.

“I’m not aware kung ano ‘yung intel report or the source of information ni Secretary Jonvic but from our sources, which we verified with the BI (Bureau of Immigration), wala kasi kaming records,” acting DOJ secretary Fredderick Vida told reporters on Wednesday, October 21.
(I’m not aware what is the intel report or the source of information of Secretary Jonvic but from our sources, which we verified with the BI, we don’t have any records.)

“So I cannot confirm that he is already out of the country kasi (because) we will rely based on what we have in immigration records, and based on immigration records, wala kaming record that he left (we don’t have records that he left),” Vida added.

This is possible, actually. If Ang indeed used backdoor exit points, then the immigration bureau would not have a record of his flight. There are alleged backdoor points in Palawan and in Mindanao, according to several reports.
Besides, Ang would and could not have used proper exit channels because it would have alerted authorities.
But whether or not Ang has already left the country, one thing remains unchanged: the police have failed and continue to fail to locate and arrest him.

The police, earlier this year, attempted to arrest him in Pasig City and in Zambales, but failed because he was not there. As of February, the DILG also raised the bounty for Ang’s arrest to P20 million, but to no avail.

blocks.caption: Where in the world is Atong Ang? Is he in the Philippines or not?

blocks.text: So who’s answerable for these failures? Who will be held accountable by the Marcos government?

“Tingnan po natin at sa ngayon ay dapat malaman natin, maimbestigahan kung talagang may lapses. So, may mga tao talaga na mabibilis tumakbo at hindi naman ito ang unang pagkakataon na tumakas itong si Atong Ang. Noong unang nakasuhan din ito, nakaalpas din ito agad-agad,” said Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro on Wednesday.

(We’ll see and for now, we should find out, investigate if there are lapses. There are people who are good at escaping and this is not the first time that Atong Ang has escaped. When he was charged, he immediately fled.) – Rappler.com

articles.title: Besieged Yemeni city on verge of ‘unmanageable’ crisis, aid workers warn
articles.summary:
Water and fresh food running out in Taiz as fighting intensifies and Houthi advance cuts off most supply routes

The humanitarian crisis in the besieged Yemeni city of Taiz is becoming…

blocks.text: The humanitarian crisis in the besieged Yemeni city of Taiz is becoming unmanageable as the city runs out of water, fuel and fresh food, Oxfam aid workers in the country have warned.

Iran-allied Houthi forces have largely encircled the city of more than 900,000 people, cutting it off from most supply routes. This week, heavy fighting has raged around the city’s old airport, causing extensive damage in a densely populated residential area.

The conflict has intensified since forces loyal to the internationally recognised government and the Saudi-led coalition launched airstrikes on the Houthi-held airport in Sana’a in July, shattering a 2022 ceasefire deal that had largely stopped the fighting.

The UN has called for aid workers to be given access to Taiz. Oxfam in London called for the UK to send extra humanitarian aid to the country. The UK has allocated just £104m in aid to Yemen for each of the next three years, down from the £196m allocated in 2020. US aid to the stricken country has been virtually wiped out, and Germany, another leading funder, has halved its aid programme.

Donor countries have subscribed to only 23% of the cost of the UN humanitarian relief programme for Yemen this year, and pressure is growing on Saudi Arabia – itself cash-strapped by the cost of war – to make up the shortfall. The World Food Programme said wheat flour reserves in the city were nearly exhausted as of mid-October.

blocks.caption: People ride past a pile of burning rubbish in Taiz. Photograph: Anees Mahyoub/Reuters

blocks.text: On Tuesday the UK government allocated an unspecified sum in extra military help to Saudi Arabia to help protect its airports and infrastructure, but London has yet to decide on whether to back a much more robust military response, including supporting the possible deployment of foreign ground troops to Yemen.
Fatma Jaffar, a Yemen-based advocacy manager for Oxfam, said local staff described an almost total siege of Taiz.

“All the main entrances [to the city] have been blocked. The clashes are continuing and the casualties are very high,” she said. “Even people that have money are not able to buy food. Supplies are becoming very limited in the markets. No fuel has entered Taiz for two or three weeks. Drinking water is a massive issue. Even our staff are struggling to buy water.

“Hospitals are struggling without medicines and a lot of people as a result are dying. Those that have been wounded by missiles – there have been attempts to get them out of the city, but because of the blockade they are not able to transfer anyone. Prices have rocketed.

“Our staff told me that people are even searching for apples right now and they cannot find any fresh fruit, and basic commodities are not found inside the city. Garbage is piling up since they are not able to transfer the waste outside the city. They are trying to burn it, but we can only anticipate there will be diseases such as cholera in the near future. If this goes on much longer and access remains blocked, there will be casualties from missiles, hunger and disease from lack of water right across the city.
“The situation was bad before the escalation – Yemen is one of the poorest countries on Earth – and now it is becoming unmanageable.”

blocks.caption: People wait to fill up cooking gas cylinders in Taiz. Photograph: Anees Mahyoub/Reuters

blocks.text: Prices have rocketed: a 20-litre container of petrol that cost about $20 (£15) before the crisis is now worth $80 on the hidden market. Potato prices have doubled.
The Houthi focus on Taiz reflects the city’s strategic importance, but the level of resistance inside the city may swallow the group’s resources, weakening its response elsewhere.
Oxfam has been forced to transfer its limited resources from development to emergency humanitarian work, including offering cash transfers.
The Halo Trust, the world’s largest humanitarian landmine-clearance organisation, said 30 of its staff were among hundreds of thousands of civilians trapped inside the city.

In the Trump administration’s fiscal year 2027 budget request to Congress, the US state department has requested no economic support or development assistance specifically for Yemen. By comparison, the US committed roughly $760m in total aid to Yemen during the last year of Joe Biden’s presidency.

UN diplomats are still mediating between the two sides, but there is no sign that either the Houthis or the internationally recognised government are ready for a ceasefire, let alone a long-term settlement.

articles.title: Russia arrests German man, calls him a Ukraine 'mercenary'
articles.summary: Russian FSB agents have arrested a German national and accused him of fighting as a mercenary for Ukraine's military. They claim he deserted over unpaid wages and say he was a sniper who once served…

image.caption: Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB) did not name the individual but did show videos and photos it purported to be himImage: Russian Federal Security Service/ITAR-TASS/IMAGO

blocks.text: Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB) domestic intelligence agency said on Wednesday that it had arrested a German national on allegations of mercenary activity, calling him an "active member of the Ukrainian armed forces."
The news came on the same day that Russia released a retired teacher from the US, Stephen Hubbard, after years in detention on similar mercenary charges, which he denied.
Russia has detained a number of foreign nationals since its 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine, accusing them of assisting Kyiv in some way or another.
There was no immediate comment from Germany's government, besides acknowledging that it had seen the reports and was pursuing them.
What did the FSB say about the arrest?

The FSB said in a statement carried widely by Russian media that the man was a former Bundeswehr soldier and trained sniper. It did not issue his name but published a short video in which he could be heard speaking German.

blocks.caption: The FSB also published footage that it said showed the man holding a sniper rifle with Ukrainian Armed ForcesImage: Russian Federal Security Service/ITAR-TASS/IMAGO

blocks.text: According to the FSB, the man was a Bundeswehr soldier from 1996 to 2010, who served in Afghanistan and Somalia between 2004 and 2010.
They alleged that he later operated as a mercenary fighter in Syria's civil war.
From 2016 to 2018, according to the Russian spy agency, he fought in Ukraine against the Russian-backed rebels in eastern states, prior to Moscow's full-scale invasion in 2022.
The FSB claimed that he returned to Ukraine as a "mercenary" in 2025 and was fighting in the contested region of Donetsk, but then deserted over non-payment of wages.
They did not comment on why or how the man, whom they said was born in 1976, had come to be in Russia. Nor did they say where or under what circumstances they arrested him.
How did German authorities respond?
A spokesperson at the German Foreign Ministry only initially responded by saying that Berlin was aware of the reports from Russia.
The spokesperson said the ministry would not comment on the individual case or specifics for the time being.
German spy chief warns of rising Russia threat
Similar Swedish arrest last week, US prisoner freed
Russia has arrested hundreds of foreign nationals on charges like espionage, sabotage and treason amid its invasion of neighboring Ukraine. The charges can carry lengthy prison sentences.
A smaller number have also been accused of mercenary activity.
The FSB last week arrested a Swedish national, again accusing him of fighting on Kyiv's behalf.
In his case, they said he was operating as the commander of a drone unit and that he was detained attempting to illegally cross the border in the western Pskov region.
A Japanese journalist was also arrested last week, accused of espionage, prompting sharp criticism from Tokyo.
Also on Wednesday, Russia released a retired US teacher, Stephen Hubbard, who had been arrested in 2024 on comparable allegations.
This took place as US negotiator Steve Witkoff was visiting St. Petersburg and after a series of recent concessions to Russia and criticisms of Ukraine from US President Donald Trump.
Trump claimed there was no quid pro quo involved in the release, but later said Hubbard would not be free if he had not eased sanctions on Russian diesel shipments.

articles.title: Lacson calls out Cayetanos for hijacking DENR budget hearing
articles.summary: Senators Alan Peter and Pia Cayetano take turns grilling LLDA Acting General Manager Leopoldo Parumog over his supposed 'special interest' in reclamation projects in Taguig

blocks.text: PING LACSON. Senator Ping Lacson at the briefing on the proposed 2027 budget of the Department of National Defense on October 19, 2026.
Senate of the Philippines
Senators Alan Peter and Pia Cayetano take turns grilling LLDA Acting General Manager Leopoldo Parumog over his supposed 'special interest' in reclamation projects in Taguig

The subject of the ongoing spat between senators Alan Peter Cayetano and Panfilo “Ping” Lacson — Taguig’s “ghost projects” — found its way to the Senate hearing on the proposed 2027 budget of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), where the Cayetano senator-siblings subjected the Laguna Lake Development Authority (LLDA) representative to intense questioning.

During the budget hearing of the DENR, which oversees the LLDA, Alan and his sister, Senator Pia Cayetano, took turns grilling LLDA Acting General Manager Leopoldo Parumog over what they alleged to be his “special interest” in Taguig City, the Cayetanos’ baliwick.

At the October 19 budget hearing, the Cayetanos questioned Parumog over the LLDA’s inspection of projects along Laguna de Bay, accusing him of singling out Taguig City by publicly disclosing their investigations into the reclamation projects. Taguig Mayor Lani Cayetano is Alan’s wife.

“Why do you make it appear in public that a lot of bad things are happening in Taguig? And if you don’t — if that is not the intention, then why publicize for Taguig and you don’t publicize your work in other places?” asked Pia.
According to Alan, while the LLDA issued cease-and-desist orders against projects in Angono, Rizal, and Muntinlupa City these were not publicized.
Parumog denied that the LLDA’s actions on Taguig projects were politically motivated.
“There is no politics involved. We are not selective and we act on everything,” Parumog said in Filipino.
The Cayetano siblings’ questioning did not sit well with Lacson, who called them out for turning the budget deliberations into a “full-blown” Senate investigation.

“They took turns interrogating the hapless LLDA general manager with questions totally unrelated to the agency’s proposed 2027 budget as if it were a full-blown Senate inquiry in aid of legislation,” Lacson said in a statement on Tuesday, October 20.
The latest clash adds another layer to the feud between Lacson and Alan, which began in July when Lacson questioned the increase in the minority leader’s declared net worth in 2025.

The dispute has since intersected with allegations of irregularities in flood control projects in Taguig, with Lacson — former Senate blue Ribbon committee chairperson — turning over to the Ombudsman the evidence the panel had gathered on the alleged anomalies.
This is not the first time an individual was caught in the crossfire between the two senators.
In September, Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon found himself in a similar situation after he denied in a Senate budget hearing that there were ghost projects in Taguig City.
Lacson had previously said his team identified at least 32 allegedly anomalous flood control projects in Taguig, two of which were considered as ghost projects.
After his denial, Lacson said Dizon apologized for his remarks. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Macron accuses foreign leaders of exploiting French riots
articles.summary: The comment is an apparent swipe at Benjamin Netanyahu and Donald Trump, who both face elections in coming weeks.
articles.byline: Patrick Jackson, Marco Silva, Thomas Copeland

blocks.text: Image source, AFP via Getty Images
Violence raged in Marseille along with other French cities
ByPatrick JacksonMarco Silva and Thomas CopelandBBC Verify
French President Emmanuel Macron has accused foreign leaders of exploiting the riots which erupted across the country on Saturday for electoral purposes.
Without naming them, he said they were campaigning for forthcoming elections "at France's expense" with their comments on the violence, which erupted on the fringe of cost-of-living protests.
Speaking on a visit to the Middle East, he referred to them as "leaders who are in campaign mode, whether here in the region or on the other side of the Atlantic".
It was an apparent swipe at Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who faces parliamentary elections next week, and US President Donald Trump, for whom mid-term polls fall next month.
Macron said the unnamed leaders had been influenced by fake videos generated by AI about the riots.
Nearly 150 people have been jailed and more than 800 brought before the courts since the riots which gripped Paris and other cities including Lyon, Marseille and Nice.
Video of running battles between masked rioters and police, as well as property being destroyed and stores being looted, spread across social media.
The government admitted the police had "lost control" during the violence, which came after weeks of protests by students over conditions in high schools.
Macron vowed afterwards that the authorities would be "uncompromising" towards "agitators from ultra-left fringe groups", which he blamed for much of the trouble.

Speaking in the Qatari capital Doha, the French president said: "For me, there is no visible foreign interference in the events that took place. On the other hand, there was foreign manipulation of information afterwards, yes, and that gave rise to unacceptable and stupid comments from many people, including foreign leaders...
"We had people claiming that we had been invaded by hordes of migrants and Islamists, which is completely false."
On Tuesday, Netanyahu said in an interview for Israel's i24 channel, external that France, which has Western Europe's largest Muslim minority, had been hit by an "invasion of extremist Islam".
He said he had told Macron after the Hamas attack on Israel on 7 October 2023: "If we do not eliminate them here, you will have them in Paris." "That is exactly what is happening," he added.
Also on Tuesday, Trump blamed the riots on mass immigration to France.

"When I look at France, when you look at Italy, when you look at all the turmoil and the hatred, that's not about school," he said. "That's about people coming into the countries that hate the country."
"Close your borders and take control before it is too late!" he said in remarks directed at Macron.

According to a report in the UK's Financial Times newspaper, external, EU regulators are examining possible foreign online interference and disinformation campaigns around the French riots and similar recent outbursts of unrest in EU states.

It quotes unnamed security officials as saying that pro-Russian and far-right social media accounts linked to previous disinformation campaigns have spread violent videos in an attempt to sow more chaos.
Iran and Algeria are also suspected of being behind some of the messaging, the paper adds.

David Colon, a researcher at France's Sciences Po university who specialises in disinformation, was quoted as saying that "pro-Kremlin influencers" linked to the Russian campaign Storm-1516 had "amplified the events and spread a number of false narratives".

France is one of Ukraine's most vociferous military supporters in its ongoing war with Russia, while Algeria is a former French colony with bitter memories of its war to achieve independence in 1962, and French relations with Iran have been strained by its war with the US and Israel this year.
BBC Verify has reviewed more than 15 examples of fake news videos on social media which researchers at the US-based dTeam say are the work of a Russian disinformation operation known as Matryoshka.
The videos feature near-identical branding to real news outlets in France, including Le Monde, Euronews and France 24.
The individual impact and reach of videos made by Matryoshka appear to be limited, but experts have said the focus on amplifying unrest is consistent with known Russian disinformation tactics.

blocks.caption: A fake image of an elderly couple being robbed and left in their underwear

blocks.text: Separately, BBC Verify has traced one of the most viral AI-generated images circulating on social media, which supposedly shows an elderly couple being robbed and left in their underwear in Paris, to an obscure website.
The director of Infos-Israel.News, Sabrina Hania, told the BBC her team had created the image - which was published on 17 October - using ChatGPT without using a reference image.

It was posted shortly after a television journalist reported on the alleged incident, citing "police information". The claim remains unconfirmed, with French media reporting that prosecutors have no information supporting it having happened.
While the original image was labelled as "Made with AI" on X and "AI content" on Instagram, it was later shared on X without any disclaimer in a post which attracted more than six million views.
Hania said she regretted that the image had been taken out of context and had misled so many people, blaming those who reshared it without identifying it as AI-generated.

articles.title: El Niño ‘wrecking ball’ could cause record Pacific temperature rise, UN says
articles.summary: In Southeast Asia, warmer conditions and a lack of rainfall could impact agriculture and water supplies, while Latin America could see increased rainfall, according to the World Meteorological…

blocks.text: EL NIÑO. Tropical Storm Rachel and El Niño fueled Kelvin waves pound the boardwalk in Long Beach, California, US, on October 10, 2026.
David Swanson/Reuters

In Southeast Asia, warmer conditions and a lack of rainfall could impact agriculture and water supplies, while Latin America could see increased rainfall, according to the World Meteorological Organization

items: The El Niño weather pattern is expected to cause a record rise in ocean temperatures, with predictions of a 3.8 degrees Celsius increase in the central Pacific between November and January.
This event will likely lead to extreme weather conditions globally, including floods in southern Africa and droughts in Southeast Asia, impacting agriculture and water supplies.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

GENEVA, Switzerland – The El Niño weather pattern could cause a record rise in ocean temperatures in the Pacific as it barrels around the globe like a “wrecking ball,” causing floods and droughts, UN officials said on Wednesday, October 21.

The new World Meteorological Organization (WMO) seasonal outlook predicted the El Niño event would become extremely strong, with temperatures in the central Pacific rising about 3.8 degrees Celsius above normal between November and January, peaking around December.

“We have not seen in our records 3.8. We have seen around 3 in some record El Niños before, with very substantive impacts across the world. So we are beyond that limit,” WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo said.

blocks.caption: ‘Supersized’ El Niño may become strongest ever recorded, UN says

blocks.text: El Niño is the warm phase of the naturally occurring El Niño-Southern Oscillation cycle — a climate pattern that influences weather around the world.
It tends to cause higher global temperatures and disrupt rainfall patterns across large regions, meaning drought in some areas and heavy rains in others.
It is a natural climate pattern and is not caused by climate change. However, global warming can make El Niños more intense.
El Niño-linked weather extremes could worsen pressure on housing, water, sanitation and health services, with flooding risks rising in southern Africa from November, the WMO said.
In Southeast Asia, warmer conditions and a lack of rainfall could impact agriculture and water supplies, while Latin America could see increased rainfall, according to the WMO.
The WMO and the UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs and Emergency Relief Coordinator, Tom Fletcher, called for urgent action to get ready.

“This El Niño is the behemoth; it is a wrecking ball. It will tear through Latin America, Eastern and Southern Africa, Asia and the Pacific with extreme heat, droughts, and floods,” Fletcher said, warning of massive humanitarian consequences.
Some 50 million people could face increased hunger, he said. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Next UN chief must prove that global cooperation works, says DFA
articles.summary: The Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) on Wednesday said that the next United Nations (UN) Secretary-General must prove that international cooperation still works amid rising geopolitical tensions.

blocks.text: Published October 21, 2026 10:01pm
The Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) on Wednesday said that the next United Nations (UN) Secretary-General must prove that international cooperation still works amid rising geopolitical tensions.
DFA Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro said that the UN was founded on a simple and powerful promise: that every nation, regardless of its size and strength, had a voice.

“The next Secretary General must do more than lead an institution. The next Secretary General must help restore faith in multilateralism itself, bridging divisions, defending the UN Charter and demonstrating that international cooperation could still deliver meaningful results,” Lazaro said in the DFA’s commemoration of UN Day.
“It is our hope to call upon the United Nations to renew its purpose, restore confidence in its institutions and uphold the principles upon which it was founded,” Lazaro said.
According to Lazaro, the UN stood at a turning point amid geopolitical tensions and challenges to international law.
The very principles of the UN were also being tested, as well as the world’s confidence in its ability to implement them.

“The question is no longer simply whether the United Nations remains relevant, it's whether it can remain effective in a world that increasingly questions the value of multilateralism itself. This is what makes the selection of the next UN Secretary General so consequential,” Lazaro said.
Lazaro said that the Philippines had a high stake in the UN, as it has long championed peaceful resolutions to international disputes.
“We know that a strong United Nations is not merely desirable; it is indispensable. Especially for nations whose security rests not on power, but on principle,” Lazaro said.
The DFA’s commemoration also saw a panel discussion which included Kabataan Partylist Renee Co, The Straits Times journalist Mara Cepeda and People’s Budget Coalition organizer Kenneth Abante.
Various diplomats were also in attendance.
A new Secretary-General will be selected in the remaining months of 2026 and will assume office in 2027, replacing António Guterres of Portugal. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Australian politicians say they are paying thousands for their own security upgrades amid rising threats
articles.summary:
Home and office safety a common concern in Australian federal police and Asio safety briefings with politicians following alleged attack on MP Helen Haines

  • Get our

blocks.text: Security agencies will review safety precautions for MPs’ homes and offices after numerous federal politicians told police and Asio in safety briefings that they were worried about widening threats after the alleged attack on Helen Haines.

The Labor government and politicians across the parliament are still considering how they will respond when they return to Canberra next week, with ideas being floated including a new committee on MPs’ safety, greater resources for police, and motions of condolence for Haines, who lost both her legs after Monday’s incident. Renewed calls from the crossbench for reforms to question time and the tone of debate in parliament are unlikely to be taken up by the major parties.

In safety briefings with the Australian federal police and Asio granted to Labor, Coalition and crossbench MPs on Wednesday, security of homes and electorate offices was a common concern, according to Guardian Australia interviews with 10 MPs. While a broad review of safety and security is unlikely at this stage, multiple MPs across the political spectrum told Guardian Australia they had spent thousands of dollars of their own money to install safety features based on the advice of the federal police.

Federal ministers receive stronger security assistance, but numerous backbenchers said they felt under-resourced, saying many angry constituents may see all politicians as a homogenous group, and may not differentiate between cabinet members and ordinary local MPs.
“People are getting activated now because they see us as part of the government. We represent the system to them, as much as anyone else,” independent Monique Ryan said.

Two years ago, the AFP recorded 951 reports of harassing and threatening behaviour against office holders. Last year, that increased to 1,067. On Wednesday, police arrested a man after he allegedly caused a disturbance at a Perth electorate office and was reported to have made verbal threats “while in possession of what has been described as nunchucks”. No one was injured as a result, Western Australia police said.
‘Not well protected’

A number of politicians asked to speak anonymously to discuss reflections from the briefings. While many praised the AFP’s response when their staff contacted them – for instance, to seek advice on holding public events – some said they had received less timely assistance from local police when they requested help, such as to respond to aggressive visitors.
Numerous MPs said they did not want security guards or armed escorts for themselves in public, but that they felt alarmed for the safety of their homes and families.

Some said they would feel more comfortable with cameras and floodlights at home, and had decided to pay for their own upgrades after not being offered such features in risk assessments conducted by security agencies. One independent MP said crossbenchers questioned whether extra home security features should be paid for by the public.
Several MPs said they wanted more security and safety support, but questioned how much impact that would have on their overall safety and how much more the AFP could do.

blocks.caption: Helen Haines has lost both legs but ‘heart and mind are in good shape’, husband says – video

blocks.text: Guardian Australia was told security officials had committed to assessing safety settings of MPs who raised specific concerns. While a broad-ranging government review is at this stage not expected, other responses could include giving MPs more information on the background work that policing agencies conduct year-round, such as threat assessments and periodic checks.
The prime minister, Anthony Albanese, told News24 his government had overseen “an increase in funding for security for members of parliament in the last couple of years”.

“We want to make sure that people can feel as much comfort as possible, that everything’s being done to maximise security. But also, I think parliamentarians across the board are determined to make sure we can continue to engage as we need to in this great democracy of ours,” he said.
A spokesperson for the home affairs minister, Tony Burke, said: “Reviews of the threats faced by high office holders are constantly conducted by our agencies.”
after newsletter promotion

Ryan, who is close with Haines, said she had rarely discussed safety arrangements with fellow MPs until recent times, but claimed many colleagues were “now realising they’re having common experiences”. She was supportive of a broader review into safety, and more resources to secure offices.
“If it makes my team feel better and safer to have bollards out the front, I’m happy,” she said.

Two Labor MPs said some government backbenchers had expressed frustrations towards the finance department for not adequately funding safety measures for their electorate offices or doing so in a timely way. One said money was “always an issue” with the department, and expected more MPs to be directly lobbying the prime minister to improve office security.

Nationals MP Sam Birrell, whose electorate neighbours Haines’s in Indi, said regional politicians had particular concerns, with many being highly visible in their communities and locals often knowing where they lived.
“Some of the MPs were frustrated there’s not clear advice on things like whether to advertise mobile offices or have signs on cars,” he said.
“There were some complaints about whether people are able to get fairly modest security measures … that needs to be reviewed.”
Multiple people across meetings raised concerns about how to protect electorate office staff.
Liberal senator James Paterson told Radio National electorate offices were “very exposed” and were “not well protected”.
Asio and AFP have been contacted for comment.

articles.title: Majority of Australians who report penicillin allergy not truly allergic
articles.summary:
Peak body for immunologists changes guidelines as evidence shows up to 90% of those reporting allergy don’t have one

  • Get our

blocks.text: The majority of Australians who report a penicillin allergy are not truly allergic, prompting the peak body for immunologists to change its guidelines in a bid to reduce hospitals stays and tackle antimicrobial resistance.
Penicillin, one of the most commonly prescribed antibiotics in Australia, was thought to cause allergies in 10% of Australians, or about 2.8 million people.
But the latest evidence shows up to 90% of those reporting a penicillin allergy do not have one.

The changes to the Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy guidelines, which have been published in the Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology, give the first peer-reviewed and updated advice to GPs and other health professionals about how to diagnose and manage the allergy, and when to refer to a specialist.

Prof Michaela Lucas, a clinical immunologist, said misdiagnosis occurs for a number of reasons, with people sometimes experiencing a rash or nausea after taking penicillin and assuming it’s an allergy, or doctors wanting to be cautious and recording side-effects as allergies.

Other people were told by a parent that they suffered a reaction when they were a child and carry that diagnosis through to adulthood without questioning it, she said, while some side-effects may also be due to the illness itself and not the medicine.
Penicillin is an important antibiotic option, as it treats common infections, said Lucas, a professor at the University of Western Australia’s medical school.
“It is also what is known as a narrow spectrum antibiotic, which means it is targeted at the bug specifically causing the infection,” she said.

“Once you have to avoid narrow classes of drugs, you have to use broader spectrum antibiotics which have a bigger impact of your gut microbiome as they are associated with also killing good bacteria and allowing superbugs to come in and take residency.”
Superbugs are strains of bacteria that are highly resistant to multiple standard treatments.
“Antimicrobial resistance matters beyond the individual patient, because resistant bacteria can spread between people and through communities,” Lucas said.
“If someone develops a serious infection that is resistant to several antibiotics, doctors can be left with very limited treatment options.”

Dr Nick Cooling, the chair of the Royal Australian College of General Practitioners’ allergy special interest group, said the guidelines were based on the latest evidence, and a consensus report from a range of medical specialities.
He hopes the guidance will cut health costs in the community and ease the burden on immunologists.
“We know that people who have a penicillin allergy label go to hospital more,” he said.
after newsletter promotion
“They spend longer in hospital, and they also cost the system more.”
This is because of more treatments needing to be trialled, side-effects from those treatments, and delays in finding alternative treatments.
“The ability to clarify that with these patients will reduce hospital costs but also the whole health system cost,” he said.
“We need all health professionals to be involved in this because if we’re going to de-label some 2.8 million people in Australia, you can’t just rely on the 300 immunologists to do that.”

Cooling urged affected patients to raise the question of a penicillin allergy with their GP, and with cases where the potential risk of harm is low, doctors could give their patient penicillin and monitor for symptoms.
But he warned: “No one should try taking penicillin themselves to find out whether they are allergic. Antibiotics should only be taken when prescribed for the individual taking them.”
For Tammy Prescino, the issue of penicillin allergy is a very real concern. She welcomes the changes, with her 70-year-old mother and 12-year-old daughter both diagnosed.
Prescino worries that if her mother were to get an infection, she could miss out on the benefits of penicillin. She plans to see a doctor and to get her family reassessed.
“Because if she doesn’t have the penicillin allergy, then we wouldn’t have to withhold medicine … that could help her,” Prescino said.

articles.title: Severely ill ICE detainees targeted for imminent deportation in Florida, advocates say
articles.summary:
Flights to unknown countries in Africa are scheduled as early as Wednesday, relatives detail

Relatives of gravely ill detainees at two

blocks.text: Relatives of gravely ill detainees at two Florida immigration jails say authorities are about to deport their loved ones to unknown countries in Africa despite worsening medical conditions.

Flights are scheduled as early as Wednesday, according to the families and the immigration advocacy group the Workers Circle, which has been monitoring conditions and speaking with detainees inside two Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facilities in south Florida.
The group said multiple sick detainees with varying conditions have been targeted for imminent deportation, and learned about the operation only in the last few days.

“I received a call from several detainees letting me know that men were being pulled in to interviews with deportation agents, where they were being informed that because of their medical conditions, Mexico would not be accepting their entry, and they will be sent to Africa,” Arianne Betancourt, the group’s immigrant rights organizer, said at a Tuesday night press conference.
“We know that once they are deported and sent to these third countries, they are not receiving medical care in detention. They have difficulties getting medicine.”

The affected detainees are at the Krome North processing center in Miami, which was found to be experiencing severe overcrowding by a government inspector’s report last month, and the Broward transitional center in Pompano Beach. Both facilities are privately run on behalf of ICE.

Anisley Cortés, the wife of Noslén Sendra, a 41-year-old Cuban national, said her husband has been incarcerated since last November, first at the now closed “Alligator Alcatraz” immigration jail, and at Krome since April. She said he has uncontrolled diabetes and acute pancreatitis that resulted in a weeks-long hospital stay earlier this year.

“He lost over 50 pounds. They wouldn’t give him his medication, and they would not give him enough food. It was a nightmare of a time for all of us,” she said. “He is very sick and needs the right healthcare.

“Cuba will not accept him as a deportee, and we now have proof that Mexico will not accept him as a deportee because he is so sick. And so they told him that because he could not be accepted at either of those two countries, ‘Oh well, we’re going to have to send you to Africa’.

“They told him that Mexico would not accept him because he has too many medications that he requires, and so they said, ‘Well, we have to deport you anyway’. We’re left with the uncertainty of not knowing how he is, or if we’ll see him again.”
Shalyn Fluharty, an immigration rights attorney, said information from the detainees indicated deportation flights were imminent.

“We understand that just this week, within a couple of days, likely Thursday and Friday, there will be two flights going to Africa, in particular to the Central African Republic, and we also believe Burundi,” she said.
Fluharty said previously deported immigrants were shackled at their hands, ankles and waists during lengthy flights, and some who complained were placed in full body wraps with no ability to move.
“This is what we anticipate will be happening this week for these individuals, based upon what we’ve seen in the past,” she said.

“Travel can last sometimes up to 24 hours. What if you’re somebody who has a heart condition? Who has a high risk of stroke? Who is experiencing diabetes and requires regular access to food or insulin? These conditions take your already vulnerable medical state and make them, unfortunately, often life-threatening.”

Responding to a request for comment, a spokesperson for the homeland security department demanded to know the affected detainees’ personal information. The department did not respond further when provided with Sendra’s details.
Betancourt said families risked retaliation for their relatives by coming forward. “This is not a single one-off story,” she said.

“The inspector general’s report confirmed that there is a lack of medical care inside of the Krome detention facility. Families have been demanding oversight, and every day they are experiencing real fear to speak up and advocate for their loved ones.”

During two unannounced visits to Krome in May, government inspectors found multiple violations of noncompliance with detention standards, including severe overcrowding. Holding 1,102 detainees in a facility with a maximum capacity of 882, the report said, “jeopardizes the safe and orderly operations within the facility”.

Other listed violations included an inadequate number of operational toilets, sinks, and showers, and previous complaints included female detainees made to use toilets in full view of men, and arriving detainees held for more than 24 hours in a bus in the parking lot because of a lack of space.

Advocates say Donald Trump’s massive second term immigration crackdown has caused overcrowding in detention centers nationwide that DHS has attempted to alleviate by ramping up deportation flights to so-called third countries.
The controversial practice, approved by the US supreme court last month, has seen hundreds of detainees deported to at least a dozen African countries where they have no ties.

A Human Rights Watch report earlier this month found countless examples of abusive treatment during and after the flights, and detainees subjected to persecution, arbitrary incarceration and torture following their arrival.

articles.title: Family of prison officer killed by IRA receives state apology
articles.summary: Brian Stack was crossing a street in Dublin in 1983 when he was shot in the back of the neck and died 18 months later.

blocks.text: Image source, Handout
Brian Stack was shot in the back of the neck as he left a boxing match in 1983
ByFiona Murray
BBC News NI
The family of a senior Irish prison officer murdered by the IRA has received a state apology on Wednesday for failings in investigations into his killing.
Brian Stack, a father of three, was crossing a street in Dublin, after leaving a boxing match in 1983, when he was shot in the back of the neck.
Stack, who was the chief prison officer at the high-security Portlaoise Prison, was left paralysed and died 18 months later, aged 49.
There were three separate garda (Irish police) investigations into Stack's death, but no-one was brought to justice for his killing.
Taoiseach (Irish prime minister) Micheál Martin offered an apology on behalf of the state during a sitting of the Dáil (Irish parliament).
Stack's wife Sheila and her sons Austin, Kieran and Oliver were in the Dáil chamber for the apology.
Martin said the Provisional IRA is "still in the possession of all the facts" on this case.
Apology means 'an awful lot'
Speaking to BBC Radio Ulster's Good Morning Ulster programme Brian Stack's son, Austin Stack, said the apology "means an awful lot to us".
"It's a great sense of comfort, to particularly my mother and to myself and my two brothers, because the state is officially owning up to the errors and the missions that happened," he said.
He went on to say that the serious crime review team looked into the first investigation and "they found 194 errors and omissions".
"So I have, and my family have, met with several ministers for justice down through the years and we have a requested sight of that report.
"And every time we've requested it, we've been told that it's an internally valid document and that we cannot see it."
Austin Stack said that Wednesday would be a very emotional day for his family.
"My dad was doing a very difficult job at a very difficult time in our history," he said.
"He was awarded the Irish Prison Service's highest bravery award for that work that he was doing. And this is further vindication of him and his good name."
Prior to the Dáil proceedings, the Stack family held a private meeting at government buildings with the taoiseach and Minister for Justice Jim O'Callaghan.
'Utterly unacceptable'

blocks.caption: Image caption, Taoiseach Micheál Martin formally apologised to the Stack family

blocks.text: Image source, PA Media
Taoiseach Micheál Martin formally apologised to the Stack family
In 2007 the Garda Commissioner directed a review of the case by the Garda Serious Crime Review Team. Over 200 recommendations were made relating to the cases.
This review led to "serious failings" being found as well as "the shortcomings in the management" of the earlier Garda investigation.

These failures, listed by Martin in the Dáil, are: failure to keep a map made of the crime scene, a failure to keep a motorbike helmet found near the crime scene and linked to the crime, a failure to keep custody of material exhibits, including various fingerprints, samples and debris gathered during the investigation.

The taoiseach also said there was a failure to document some potentially important aspects of the original investigation, including whether Brian's colleagues at Portlaoise Prison were interviewed and whether prisoners at the prison were interviewed.
There was also a failure to interview the Stack family and to interview Brian's wider group of friends.
"It is plainly and utterly unacceptable that material that was potentially of evidential value to the investigation can no longer be located by An Garda Síochána.
"It is admitted by An Garda Síochána that these are serious matters that had an impact on the investigation," Martin said.
"As Taoiseach, and on behalf of the Government, I want to formally apologise to the Stack family for these failings."

blocks.caption: Image caption, NI secretary Sir Chris Bryant was asked about the matter in the House of Commons

blocks.text: NI secretary Sir Chris Bryant was asked about the matter in the House of Commons
Speaking in the Commons during Northern Ireland questions on Wednesday, Secretary of State Sir Chris Bryant said he "warmly welcomed" the taoiseach making the apology.

Asked about the matter by Democratic Unionist Party leader Gavin Robinson, Sir Chris said Dublin doing so was "entirely right and proper" and went to the heart of discussions MPs had been having this week as they debated the government's Troubles legacy bill.
He added that it was "incumbent on all of us to make fulsome and not mealy-mouthed apologies".
'Regret'
The IRA admitted killing Stack in 2013 after his family mounted a long campaign to secure the admission, and met Sinn Féin's Gerry Adams and a former IRA commander.
Adams, at that time, expressed his "regret" to the Stack family over the killing.
A Sinn Féin spokesperson said that "in a 2013 statement, a former IRA leader acknowledged that IRA volunteers were responsible for Brian Stack's killing".

"The statement said the shooting had not been authorised by the IRA leadership, accepted IRA responsibility for his death, said it should not have happened and expressed sorrow for the pain and hurt suffered by the family."

The spokesperson added: "As republicans, we acknowledge the hurt caused by republican actions. That suffering cannot be disowned. We are sorry for all the lives lost during the period of conflict on this island, without exception."

blocks.caption: Image caption, Irish foreign affairs minister Helen McEntee said the Provisional IRA "are responsible"

blocks.text: Irish foreign affairs minister Helen McEntee said the Provisional IRA "are responsible"
Irish foreign affairs minister Helen McEntee also spoke during the State apology, she said: "The State failed you during their investigation into Brian's killing."
She said Brian was "targeted" by the Provisional IRA and said "they are responsible".

"To Sheila and to all of the Stack family, we are deeply sorry for all that you have endured, for the failures of the investigation and the additional suffering they have caused you, we are deeply sorry. I hope today's formal apology brings some measure of peace and comfort."
Donegal Sinn Féin TD (member of Irish parliament) Pearse Doherty said the Stack's family "long search for answers deserves respect".
"No apology can restore Brian Stack's life or return the years spent seeking answers but it can recognise the wrong done."
He said the failures of the garda investigation "compounded" the suffering of the Stack family.
In 2019, the family received an apology from then garda commissioner Drew Harris in relation to the handling of the investigation into the murder.
In 2023, gardaí told the family that the file on the case - which was with the DPP (Director of Public Prosecutions) - was being sent back to police for further investigation.
Stack was the only prisoner officer in the state killed by violence related to the Troubles in Northern Ireland.

articles.title: Israeli military detains US politician Brad Lander and rabbis at olive harvest
articles.summary:
About 80 US, Israeli and British volunteers held near Nahalin in West Bank and taken to police station

The Israeli military has detained about 80 US, Israeli and British volunteers helping…

blocks.text: The Israeli military has detained about 80 US, Israeli and British volunteers helping Palestinians harvest olives near Bethlehem, including the New York Democratic congressional nominee Brad Lander, several rabbis and Israel’s former deputy attorney general.

“I’ve been detained by the IDF, along with a group of rabbis and volunteers,” Lander posted from a bus taking him to a police station. “We were simply harvesting olives in a grove near Nahalin in the West Bank. The occupation is a crime under international law. Harvesting olives isn’t a crime under any law I know.”

Lander, who is Jewish and an outspoken critic of the Israeli government, describes himself as a liberal Zionist. He believes in the vision of Israel as a safe, Jewish home, but argues that it cannot be a true democracy while it denies Palestinians their human rights and freedom.
Allow content provided by a third party?

This article includes content hosted on platform.x.com. We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as the provider may be using cookies and other technologies. To view this content, click 'Allow and continue'.
An ally of the New York City mayor, Zohran Mamdani, Lander’s critical approach to Israel was a key factor in his resounding primary victory against Dan Goldman, a prominent supporter of Israel.

He condemns Israel’s continued occupation of the West Bank and Gaza, supported the restriction of US military aid to Israel and believes that Israel’s military campaign in Gaza after the 7 October 2023 Hamas attacks amounts to genocide.
Settler militants have unleashed extreme violence on Palestinians attempting to harvest olives from their trees across the occupied West Bank, and anyone accompanying them.

A vicious assault on a US photojournalist and attacks on European diplomats and a French mayor over the weekend drew international condemnation and calls for the Israeli government to crack down on militants.
Wednesday’s olive-picking from trees outside the village of Nahalin was uneventful until a large contingent of Israeli security forces arrived, the organisers Protect the Harvest said in a statement.

“All volunteers were peacefully harvesting on the private land of a Palestinian family who had invited them. For reasons that remain unclear, the Israeli army showed up and detained approximately 80 people who were present.”

Soldiers said the area had been declared a closed military zone, separated the group by nationality and drove them to a nearby police station in minibuses for the Israelis and a larger bus for Americans.
Joshua Schoffman, who served as Israel’s deputy attorney general for more than a decade, described the mass detention as a “complete hallucination” in a post on social media.

“Just now, they told me that I’m being detained for the crime of olive harvesting,” he wrote. “We were asked to stop, and everyone complied. There was no friction whatsoever with settlers or with the security forces.”

Lander was released with a warning but all the others were still being held, Protect the Harvest said. Detainees include Jill Jacobs, the chief executive of T’ruah: The Rabbinic Call for Human Rights, and 11 other American rabbis affiliated with the group.
The detainees have been given water but no food. The Israeli military and police did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

On Monday, Lander made a first post about his journey to Palestine. “Our goals for the trip are to help protect the olive harvest – and to shed a light on the reality of the occupation,” he wrote. “Thankfully, our corner of today’s harvest was peaceful and successful. But violence unfortunately is never far away.”

articles.title: ICC Prosecution removes one incident in trial brief vs. Duterte
articles.summary: The International Criminal Court (ICC) Prosecution removed one incident from its trial brief against former president Rodrigo Duterte following the Trial Chamber"s order.

blocks.text: Published October 21, 2026 9:25pm
The International Criminal Court (ICC) Prosecution removed one incident from its trial brief against former president Rodrigo Duterte following the Trial Chamber’s order.

The ICC Prosecution and Duterte’s defense team have been discussing the evidence that the former has submitted ahead of the official opening of the trial on November 30. Duterte’s defense team has raised several concerns about the prosecution’s evidence, including its large volume.

“The Prosecution hereby provides an updated version of its Trial Brief filed 4 September 2026 (‘Trial Brief’) and Annexes C.1 and C.2 thereto, further to the Chamber's order to remove Incident 57 from the incidents included in the Trial Brief,” the prosecution said in a document from the ICC.
The ICC prosecution did not publicly disclose which case this was, as it contained sensitive information relating to witnesses.
Following the Chamber’s orders, the Prosecution said that it removed all references to Incident 57 in the Trial Brief, replacing them with “[DELETED]" to be able to cross-reference it.
“No amendments have been made to the Prosecution's List of Witnesses or its List,” the prosecution said.
According to the prosecution panel, other incidents relating to Incident 57 still had contextual elements of crimes against humanity and Duterte’s supposed criminal responsibility.
The document was signed by acting prosecutor Mame Mandiaye Niang.
Duterte is detained at the ICC in The Hague, Netherlands, for crimes against humanity in relation to the drug war.
The drug war saw at least 6,000 people dead, with rights groups believing that the number could be as high as 30,000. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: House members urge Marcos to seek Chinese envoy Jing Quan's recall
articles.summary: Ten members of the House of Representatives called on Pres. Marcos, Jr. to declare Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan persona non grata or ask China to recall him, over his reference to using force.

blocks.text: Published October 21, 2026 8:56pm

Ten members of the House of Representatives called on President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos, Jr. to declare Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan persona non grata, or ask China to recall him, over his reference to using force in relation to the Philippines.

Lawmakers led by House Senior Deputy Minority Leader Leila de Lima made the call under House Resolution 1562, saying it is in line with the Philippines’ position which renounces war as an instrument of national policy, adopts the generally accepted principles of international law as part of the law of the land and adheres to the policy of peace, equality, justice, freedom, cooperation, and amity with all nations.

“On October 15, 2026, when asked about Secretary of National Defense Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr.'s characterization of China as a regional 'troublemaker,' Ambassador Jing Quan, speaking before reporters at the Diliman Dialogues in Quezon City, declared, 'If we want to use force, we may easily win. But no, we will not use force,' further remarking that the Philippines should consider itself fortunate to have China as a neighbor because Beijing would not resort to force because it loved peace,” the Resolution read.

“Under the Constitution, the President, being vested with executive power, holds primary authority to conduct foreign relations and to represent the nation in its dealings with other states and must, therefore, take decisive action in response to statements and conduct that undermine national sovereignty and threaten the country's security,” the Resolution added.

In addition, the lawmakers cited that the Chinese Embassy in Manila addressed the members of the Senate and the House of Representatives who proposed declaring Ambassador Jing persona non grata for the aforementioned statements, daring the members of the Philippine Congress to "Just do it” and accused Filipino reporters and politicians of "exaggeration, taking things out of context, and creating hype.”

“These incidents demonstrate China's disregard for the sovereign rights of the Philippines and underscore the inconsistency between the Chinese Government's words and its actions. Now, therefore, be it resolved, that the House of Representatives urge the President of the Philippines to declare Ambassador Jing Quan of the People's Republic of China persona non grata, or, in the alternative, to request his recall by the Government of the People's Republic of China,” the Resolution said.
Other co-authors of the Resolution include:

articles.title: The night watch: the YouTubers who were guardians of a shark stuck in a South Korean canal
articles.summary:
Wearing hi-vis and carrying selfie sticks, livestreamers watched over an animal that was trapped for a month and drew more than 1.6m visitors before being guided out

In

blocks.text: In South Korea, they call them jagyeongdan, a word whose meaning sits somewhere between vigilante group and neighbourhood watch. Each night they put on hi-vis vests, picked up their selfie sticks and gathered around the harbour in Busan to keep watch over an unlikely charge: a stranded shark affectionately known as Bukang-i.

On Wednesday, after more than a month in the canal and at the third attempt, the shark was successfully guided out, South Korea’s oceans ministry said. Officials expect her to move into open water in time.
For the month that she was stranded, the group of self-appointed guardians took turns to protect her, patrolling the waterfront at night for visitors who might disturb the animal.

Most are YouTubers who livestreamed the waterway, where the shark became a national celebrity. They stayed up through the night, calling out anyone shining torches or lasers into the water. Some of their videos have been watched hundreds of thousands of times.

blocks.caption: Visitors watching the shark trapped in a waterway in the south-eastern port city of Busan. Photograph: Jung Yeon-Je/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: “They bring fishing lamps, or the kind of lights people use at a campsite,” said Choi Won-jin, one of the shark’s protectors. He would arrive as the lights went out along the canal and wait for the offenders Koreans online call “lantern villains”.

The shark had been marooned in the canal since 18 September. Named after Bukhang, the Korean name for the city’s North Port, and about 3 metres long, the female dusky shark was one of a species classed as endangered worldwide. More than 1.6 million visitors came to see her, the city said, at a park that used to draw about 2,000 people on a busy Saturday.

Authorities had twice tried to guide her back out to sea and failed. Until she left, the shark remained in the canal, drawing crowds by day and leaving a handful of men to keep watch after dark. They patrolled the canal’s park to check everything was in order, ate snacks as the night went by, and shared their grievances on air about the behaviour they witnessed.

“We’re ordinary members of the public,” said Choi, who has had a YouTube channel for 10 years and covers trending issues in South Korea. “So we have no choice but to put it nicely, and get them to understand as best we can.”

“Don’t, please don’t switch the torch on,” said one of them, a YouTuber who lived nearby and went by the name Na Tae-soo. Most people complied, he said. “The animal thrashes about at night because of the torches, and it’s dangerous.”

blocks.caption: Crowds flocked to the waterfront park in Busan to see the shark. Photograph: Yonhap/EPA

blocks.text: His footage captured the shark twisting sharply away from a beam of light at 2am and striking the side of the canal. The national institute of fisheries science later confirmed an abrasion on her snout and said a visitor’s torch was likely to have startled the shark into injury.

Korean media reported that 105 officials from seven agencies watched over her, with a team on standby to reach the water within three minutes. Choi disputed this, saying that after dark it was almost up to him and the others.

The waterfront was closed to the public from midnight until 5am, a restriction the YouTubers said was impossible to enforce across a park that size. One night, livestreaming from the walkway, Choi filmed a man tipping food waste into the water.
Nobody saw the shark feed, though experts said feeding could happen in an instant and sharks her size did not need to eat often.
Further attempts to free the shark had been paused on the grounds that more force would distress her.

Cooler water had been expected to prompt her to move on. Dusky sharks prefer water between 18C and 26C, the fisheries institute said. Experts put 15C as the point below which her physiological functions would start to decline, and about 11C as the point at which survival would become precarious. Busan city officials had expected the canal to reach that temperature after the middle of November.

blocks.caption: This aerial photo taken on 29 September shows South Korean coastguard boats spraying water in an attempt to guide the shark back to the sea.  Photograph: Yonhap/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: The fisheries institute recorded 46 large sharks off the east coast in the first half of this year, nearly four times as many as a year earlier, which it attributed to warmer seas and more of the fish that sharks feed on.

The affection for Bukang-i has meanwhile become an industry, with a commemorative soju, a baseball mascot in a shark cape and an honorary city ambassadorship, and nearby shops reporting a surge in sales. South Korea’s president, Lee Jae Myung, visited the canal in mid-October.
None of the shark’s guardians thought she should be forced out. Choi said the city should protect her where she was until she left of her own accord.

Kim Jong-hwan, who runs a small business, kept watch by day as well and livestreamed her almost every day. “I went to pass on information [to my followers], and after that I started observing her”, he said. “Watching her over time, with the water pumps being fired and then the nets, I came to find those things being done to her objectionable. So we ended up cheering her on.”

“She’s just an animal, and she came in by her own choice,” Kim said. “If it gets cold, if there’s no food, if the water doesn’t suit her, she’ll leave by herself. I’d like her to just be left alone, to rest there comfortably until then, and go.”

articles.title: Sara Duterte: Marcos, lawmakers accountable for unconstitutional national budgets
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte on Wednesday said President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. and members of Congress should be held accountable for the passage of the budget laws for 2024 and 2025, and…

blocks.text: Published October 21, 2026 7:31pm

Vice President Sara Duterte on Wednesday said President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. and members of Congress should be held accountable for the passage of the budget laws for 2024 and 2025, and part of the 2026 General Appropriations Act (GAA), which were deemed by the Supreme Court as unconstitutional.

In a statement, Duterte called out the Marcos and lawmakers following the Supreme Court's ruling in relation to irregular increases in unprogrammed appropriations (UA) that exceeded the President's proposed budget.

"Ipinagtanggol ng Korte Suprema ang batas. Ngayon, panahon na upang managot sa taumbayan si Pangulong Marcos at ang mga miyembro ng Kongreso na naglapastangan at nagpakasasa sa pera na dapat ay napunta sana sa pagpapabuti ng buhay ng mga Pilipino," Duterte said.

(The Supreme Court defended our laws. Now, it's time for President Marcos and members of Congress who violated and enriched themselves to be held accountable to the people. These funds could have been used to improve the lives of Filipinos.)

In its ruling, the Supreme Court struck down the 2024 budget because of a P449.5-billion increase in unprogrammed appropriations, while the 2025 GAA was voiced because of the additional P17.99 billion for the Special Road Fund of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH).
It also ruled as unconstitutional Special Provisions 1(a) and (b), Chapter XLIII of the 2026 GAA, which authorized unprogrammed appropriations.
Duterte was critical of Marcos' role in the budget process.

"Pinapasalamatan natin ang Korte Suprema sa pagpapatibay sa Konstitusyon at pagtitiyak na manaig ang batas, batay sa desisyon nito hinggil sa pagsabing unconstitutional ang General Appropriations Act noong 2024 at 2025, at ang bahagi ng GAA 2026. Ngayon, kailangang panagutan ni Pangulong Ferdinand Marcos Jr. ang pagpasa ng isang pambansang badyet na malinaw na taliwas sa National Expenditure Program (NEP)," Duterte said.

(We thank the Supreme Court for standing by the Constitution and ensuring that the rule of law prevailed, based on its decision regarding the unconstitutionality of the 2024, 2025 and part of the GAA 2026. Now, the President has to be held responsible for the budget that clearly went beyond the NEP.)
Duterte said the President's responsibility is clear since a budget bill would not be passed into a law unless the President signs it.

"Dapat niyang sagutin kung bakit niya nilagdaan ang isang badyet na hindi naman tumutugma sa panukala ng kanyang sariling administrasyon. Ang pambansang badyet ay pera ng taumbayan, hindi kasangkapan sa pamumulitika at personal na interes ng mga nasa puwesto sa gobyerno," the vice president added.

(The President should answer why he signed a budget that is not aligned with the proposals of his administration. The national budget is the people's money, not a tool for politics and personal interests of those in government.)
GMA News Online has requested comment from Malacañang regarding Duterte's comments, but it has yet to respond as of posting time.
Earlier in the day, Malacañang said it would ask the Supreme Court to reconsider its ruling.
The Palace said Marcos was simply adhering to existing policy and could not be held liable as he was complying with the law. — VDV, GMA News
